zajjaj:1-1.t:
From Sūrat ”اَلْمائِدَةِ“ (al-Māʾida)
﷽
His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أوْفُوا بِالعُقُودِ﴾: Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — addressed all the believers with fulfilling the contracts which Allah contracted upon them, and the contracts which they contract with one another in accordance with what the religion requires. So He said: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾, i.e. O you who have believed the Prophet ﷺ, fulfil the contracts. ”اَلْعُقُودُ“ are the covenants; one says: ”وَفَيْتُ بِالعَهْدِ“ and ”أوْفَيْتُ“ ("I fulfilled the covenant"). The singular of ”اَلْعُقُودُ“ is ”عَقْدٌ“, and they are the most binding of covenants. One says: ”عَهِدْتُ إلى فُلانٍ في كَذا وكَذا“ ("I charged so-and-so with such-and-such"), whose interpretation is: "I made that binding on him"; but if [فَإنَّما] you say: ”عاقَدْتُهُ“ or ”عَقَدْتُ عَلَيْهِ“, its interpretation is that you made that binding on him with a firm guarantee. «[Translator's note: the source reads فَإنَّما قُلْتَ; the sense requires "if/when you say" (perhaps originally فَإذا قُلْتَ).]» Some said: ”أوْفُوا بِالعُقُودِ“ means: [fulfil] what some of you contracted with others in the Jāhiliyya, such as clientage alliances (al-muwālāh), and like His saying: ﴿والَّذِينَ عَقَدَتْ أيْمانُكم فَآتُوهم نَصِيبَهُمْ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 33]; and the laws of inheritance abrogate the contracts in the matter of inheritance. One says: ”عَقَدْتُ الحَبْلَ، والعَهْدَ، فَهو مَعْقُودٌ“ ("I tied the rope / the covenant, so it is tied"). Al-Ḥuṭayʾa said:
قَوْمٌ إذا عَقَدُوا عَقْدًا لِجارِهِمُ ∗∗∗ شَدُّوا العِناجَ وشَدُّوا فَوْقَهُ الكَرَبا
(A people who, when they tie a pact for their neighbour, tighten the lower bucket-rope and tighten the cross-cord above it.)
Its interpretation is that they fulfil their covenants by being faithful to them. One also says: ”أعْقَدْتُ العَسَلَ ونَحْوَهُ، فَهو مُعْقَدٌ، وعَقِيدٌ“ ("I thickened the honey and the like, so it is thickened"); and some transmitted: ”عَقَدْتُ العَسَلَ، والكَلامَ، أعْقَدْتُ“. The poet said:
وَكَأنَّ رُبًّا أوْ كَحِيلًا مُعْقَدًا ∗∗∗ حَشَّ الوَقُودُ بِهِ جَوانِبَ قُمْقُمِ
(It is as though thick syrup, or tar boiled thick, around which the fuel was stoked against the sides of a kettle…)
His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿أُحِلَّتْ لَكم بَهِيمَةُ الأنْعامِ﴾: some said: ”بَهِيمَةُ الأنْعامِ“ are gazelles, wild cattle and wild asses. ”اَلْأنْعامُ“ in the language comprises camels, cattle and sheep/goats. So the interpretation — and Allah knows best — is: "the beasts of the livestock are made lawful for you", i.e. camels, cattle, sheep and goats, and wild game are made lawful for you. The evidence that al-anʿām comprises what we have described is His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَمِنَ الأنْعامِ حَمُولَةً وفَرْشًا﴾ [al-Anʿām: 142]: the ḥamūla are the camels that carry burdens, and the farsh are the young camels. He said: ﴿ثَمانِيَةَ أزْواجٍ مِنَ الضَّأْنِ اثْنَيْنِ ومِنَ المَعْزِ اثْنَيْنِ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 143], then He said: ﴿وَمِنَ الإبِلِ اثْنَيْنِ ومِنَ البَقَرِ اثْنَيْنِ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 144]. This is referred back to His saying: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي أنْشَأ جَنّاتٍ مَعْرُوشاتٍ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 141] — "and He produced, of the livestock, burden-bearers and small ones" — then He mentioned ”ثَمانِيَةَ أزْواجٍ“ as a badal (substitute) for His saying: ﴿وَمِنَ الأنْعامِ حَمُولَةً وفَرْشًا﴾ [al-Anʿām: 142]; and that sūra is called Sūrat ”اَلْأنْعامِ“. So these are the beasts of the livestock. They were called ”بَهِيمَةُ الأنْعامِ“ only because every living thing that does not discern is a bahīma; it was called ”بَهِيمَةٌ“ only because it is closed off (abham) from discerning. So Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known that what has been made lawful for us of the non-discerning creatures are these things.
His saying: ﴿إلا ما يُتْلى عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: the position of ”ما“ is accusative by ”إلّا“. Its interpretation is: the beasts of the livestock are made lawful for you except what is recited to you — carrion, blood, that beaten to death, that killed by a fall, and that gored. ﴿غَيْرَ مُحِلِّي الصَّيْدِ﴾, i.e. these are made lawful for you, not regarding game as lawful while you are in iḥrām. Abū al-Ḥasan al-Akhfash said: ”غَيْرُ مُحِلِّي الصَّيْدِ“ is in the accusative in connection with His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أوْفُوا بِالعُقُودِ﴾, as if it were said: "fulfil the contracts, not regarding game as lawful (غَيْرَ مُحِلِّي الصَّيْدِ)". «[Translator's note: the source writes ”غَيْرُ“ with ḍamma here, though the statement concerns its accusative.]» Some said: it is permissible for ”ما“ to be in the nominative position, on the basis that he holds that ”جاءَ إخْوَتُكَ إلّا زَيْدٌ“ is permissible; this, in the view of the Basrans, is invalid, because the meaning according to this speaker is ”جاءَ إخْوَتُكَ وزَيْدٌ“ ("your brothers came, and Zayd"), as if he uses it as a conjunction just as one conjoins with ”لا“. The Basrans permit ”جاءَ الرِّجالُ إلّا زَيْدٌ“ in the sense of ”جاءَ الرِّجالُ غَيْرُ زَيْدٍ“, on the basis that it is a naʿt (adjective) of an indefinite, or of what approximates the indefinite among generic nouns.
His saying: ﴿وَأنْتُمْ حُرُمٌ﴾, i.e. in a state of iḥrām (muḥrimūn). The singular of ”اَلْحُرُمُ“ is ”حَرامٌ“; one says: ”رَجُلٌ حَرامٌ“ and ”قَوْمٌ حُرُمٌ“. The poet said:
فَقُلْتُ لَها فِيئِي إلَيْكِ فَإنَّنِي ∗∗∗ حَرامٌ وإنِّي بَعْدَ ذاكَ لَبِيبُ
(I said to her: keep yourself back, for I am in iḥrām, and moreover I am one who is calling the talbiya.)
i.e. ”مُلَبٍّ“ (one saying the talbiya).
His saying: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ يَحْكُمُ ما يُرِيدُ﴾, i.e. creation belongs to Him — Mighty and Majestic is He —; He makes lawful of it what He wills for whom He wills, and forbids what He wills.

zajjaj:2-2.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تُحِلُّوا شَعائِرَ اللَّهِ ولا الشَّهْرَ الحَرامَ ولا الهَدْيَ ولا القَلائِدَ﴾: the singular of ”اَلشَّعائِرُ“ is ”شَعِيرَةٌ“, and its meaning is: that which has been marked (ushʿira), i.e. given a sign, so as to be sent as an offering to the Sacred House of Allah. Some people said: ”شَعائِرُ اللَّهِ“ means all the acts of worship of Allah which Allah has marked out, i.e. made into signs for us. ﴿وَلا الهَدْيَ﴾: the singular of ”اَلْهَدْيُ“ is ”هَدْيَةٌ“, like ”جَدْيَةٌ“ and ”جَدْيٌ“, meaning the pad (ḥadaba) of the saddle. ”اَلْقَلائِدُ“ (the garlands): they used to garland [themselves and their animals] with the bark of trees and seek protection by that. All of this belonged to the polytheists, and the Muslims had been commanded not to violate these things by which the polytheists drew near to Allah; and likewise ﴿وَلا آمِّينَ البَيْتَ الحَرامَ﴾. All of this is abrogated; and likewise ﴿وَلا الشَّهْرَ الحَرامَ﴾, which is ”اَلْمُحَرَّمُ“ (al-Muḥarram), because fighting was lifted in it. All of that was abrogated by His saying: ﴿فاقْتُلُوا المُشْرِكِينَ حَيْثُ وجَدْتُمُوهم وخُذُوهم واحْصُرُوهم واقْعُدُوا لَهم كُلَّ مَرْصَدٍ﴾ [al-Tawba: 5].
And His saying: ﴿وَإذا حَلَلْتُمْ فاصْطادُوا﴾: this wording is a command, but its meaning is permission, because Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — forbade game to the one in iḥrām and permitted it to him when he leaves his iḥrām; it is not that it is obligatory on him to hunt when he leaves iḥrām. Like it is His saying: ﴿فَإذا قُضِيَتِ الصَّلاةُ فانْتَشِرُوا في الأرْضِ وابْتَغُوا مِن فَضْلِ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Jumuʿa: 10], whose interpretation is that it has been permitted to you after finishing the prayer. Like that in ordinary speech: ”لا تَدْخُلَنَّ هَذِهِ الدّارَ حَتّى تُؤَدِّيَ ثَمَنَها“ ("do not enter this house until you pay its price"), "so when you have paid, enter it" — its interpretation: "when you have paid, entering it has been permitted to you."
His saying: ﴿وَلا يَجْرِمَنَّكم شَنَآنُ قَوْمٍ﴾, i.e. let not the hatred of a people induce you. One says: ”شَنِئْتُهُ شَنَآنًا“, meaning "I hated him intensely". ”اَلشَّنَآنُ“ is a maṣdar (verbal noun) like ”غَلى، غَلَيانًا“ and ”نَزا، نَزَوانًا“. So the meaning is: let not the hatred of a people earn you [the sin of] transgressing (أنْ تَعْتَدُوا). The position of ”أنْ“ is accusative, i.e. "[that] you transgress because they barred you from the Sacred Mosque (لِأنْ صَدُّوكم)". So the position of the first ”أنْ“ «[Translator's note: i.e. أنْ صَدُّوكُمْ, which precedes in the verse]» is accusative as a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), and the position of the second ”أنْ“ «[Translator's note: i.e. أنْ تَعْتَدُوا]» is accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The meaning is: "let not the hatred of a people — i.e. your hatred of a people — earn you transgression, because of their barring you from the Sacred Mosque." One says: ”فُلانٌ جَرِيمَةُ أهْلِهِ“, i.e. he is their earner. It is said in the exegesis: "let not the hatred of a people induce you", and the meaning is the same. Al-Akhfash said: "let not the hatred of a people make it your right (لا يَحِقَّنَّ لَكم)". These are different wordings, and the meaning is one.
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَتَعاوَنُوا عَلى البِرِّ والتَّقْوى﴾. All of this is abrogated except the mutual help of the Muslims in righteousness (البَرِّ). «[Translator's note: the source vocalises البَرِّ here; the verse has البِرِّ.]»

zajjaj:3-3.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمُ المَيْتَةُ﴾: its origin is ”اَلْمَيِّتَةُ“ with the doubled yāʾ, except that it is lightened; had it been read ”اَلْمَيِّتَةُ“, it would be permissible. One says ”مَيِّتٌ“ and ”مَيْتٌ“, and the meaning is the same. Some said: ”اَلْمَيِّتُ“ is said of what has not yet died, and ”اَلْمَيْتُ“ of what has already died; this is a mistake. ”مَيِّتٌ“ is valid for what has died and for what will die; Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿إنَّكَ مَيِّتٌ وإنَّهم مَيِّتُونَ﴾ [al-Zumar: 30]. And the poet said, confirming that ”اَلْمَيْتُ“ and ”اَلْمَيِّتُ“ have one meaning:
لَيْسَ مَن ماتَ فاسْتَراحَ بِمَيْتٍ ∗∗∗ إنَّما المَيْتُ مَيِّتُ الأحْياءِ
(The one who died and found rest is not dead; the dead one is only the dead among the living.)
So he made ”اَلْمَيْتُ“ a lightened form of ”اَلْمَيِّتُ“.
His saying: ﴿والدَّمُ﴾: it is said that they used to put blood into intestines, roast them and eat them; so Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known that blood poured out (al-masfūḥ), i.e. shed, is unlawful; as for what is smeared with blood, it is like the meat in being lawful.
His saying: ﴿وَما أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ بِهِ﴾: its position is nominative, and the meaning is: "and forbidden to you is what has been dedicated to other than Allah". The meaning of ”أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ بِهِ“ is: the name of other than Allah was mentioned over it. We have explained that al-ihlāl is raising the voice with something; so whatever is offered as a means of nearness — slaughtering for other than Allah, or mentioning a name other than His — is unlawful. And the flesh of swine is unlawful: Allah forbade eating it and owning it; and "swine" comprises the male and the female.
His saying: ﴿والمُنْخَنِقَةُ﴾: it is the one that is strangled by its tether-loop (ribqa), i.e. by the rope with which it is tied; in whatever way it was strangled, it is unlawful.
His saying: ﴿والمَوْقُوذَةُ﴾: it is the one killed by beating. One says: ”وَقَذْتُها، أوْقِذُها، وقْذًا“ and ”أوْقَذْتُها، أُوقِذُها، إيقاذًا“, when you have battered it heavily with blows.
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿والنَّطِيحَةُ﴾: it is the one that gores or is gored and then dies.
His saying: ﴿وَما أكَلَ السَّبُعُ﴾: the position of ”ما“ is also nominative, conjoined to what precedes it.
His saying: ﴿إلا ما ذَكَّيْتُمْ﴾, i.e. except what you reached in time to slaughter properly, of these we have described. The position of ”ما“ is accusative, i.e.: these things are forbidden to you except the thing among them whose slaughter was reached in time. Every slaughter is ”ذَكاةٌ“, and the meaning of ”اَلتَّذْكِيَةُ“ is that one reaches the animal while there is still a remnant of life in it, with which the jugular veins spurt, and it convulses as the slaughtered animal convulses whose slaughter was reached in time. The people of knowledge say: if the beast of prey has pulled out the entrails, or cut open the belly so that the entrails came out with it, there is no valid slaughter for that; its interpretation is that it has reached a state in which slaughter has no effect on its life. The origin of ”اَلذَّكاءُ“ throughout the language is the completeness of a thing. Of this is dhakāʾ in age and in understanding; it is the completeness of age. Al-Khalīl said: ”اَلذَّكاءُ في السِّنِّ“ is that a year passes over [the horse] after its qurūḥ (the cutting of its last tooth), and that is the completeness of attaining full strength. Zuhayr said:
يُفَضِّلُهُ إذا اجْتَهَدُوا عَلَيْهِ ∗∗∗ تَمامُ السِّنِّ مِنهُ والذَّكاءُ
(When they push him to his utmost, his full age and maturity give him the advantage.)
And it is said: ”جَرْيُ المُذْكِياتِ غِلابٌ“ ("the running of the fully matured ones is a contest of endurance"), i.e. the running of the aged ones that have grown mature. The interpretation of completeness of age is: the peak of youth; when it falls short of that or exceeds it, it is not called ”اَلذَّكاءُ“. Dhakāʾ in understanding is that it be a complete understanding, quick in taking in. And ”ذَكَيْتُ النّارَ“ ("I kindled the fire") is only from this; its interpretation: I completed its kindling.
﴿إلا ما ذَكَّيْتُمْ﴾: what you slaughtered completely (ما أذْكَيْتُمْ ذَبْحَهُ عَلى التَّمامِ).
His saying: ﴿وَما ذُبِحَ عَلى النُّصُبِ﴾: ”اَلنُّصُبُ“ are the stones which they used to worship, namely the idols. Its singular is ”نِصابٌ“; it is also permissible for it to be singular, with its plural ”أنْصابٌ“.
His saying: ﴿وَأنْ تَسْتَقْسِمُوا بِالأزْلامِ﴾: the position of ”أنْ“ is nominative, and the meaning is: "and forbidden to you is seeking decisions by divining arrows (al-istiqsām bi-l-azlām)". The singular of al-azlām is ”زُلَمْ“ and ”زَلَمٌ“. They were arrows in the Jāhiliyya, on some of which was written "My Lord has commanded me" and on others "My Lord has forbidden me". When a man intended a journey or a matter about which he was very concerned, he cast those arrows: if the arrow bearing "My Lord has commanded me" came out, he went ahead with his need; and if the one bearing "My Lord has forbidden me" came out, he did not go ahead with his affair. So Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known that this is unlawful. There is no difference between that and the saying of astrologers: "Do not go out because of such-and-such a star" and "Go out because of the rising of such-and-such a star", because Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿وَما تَدْرِي نَفْسٌ ماذا تَكْسِبُ غَدًا﴾ [Luqmān: 34]. It is related from the Prophet ﷺ: «"Five things none knows but Allah…", and he mentioned the verse at the end of Sūrat Luqmān: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ عِنْدَهُ عِلْمُ السّاعَةِ ويُنَـزِّلُ الغَيْثَ ويَعْلَمُ ما في الأرْحامِ وما تَدْرِي نَفْسٌ ماذا تَكْسِبُ غَدًا وما تَدْرِي نَفْسٌ بِأيِّ أرْضٍ تَمُوتُ﴾ [Luqmān: 34]». This is an intrusion into the knowledge of Allah which is unseen, and it is unlawful, like the divining arrows which Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — mentioned as unlawful. Seeking decisions by divining arrows is fisq (depravity); ”اَلْفِسْقُ“ is a name for everything which Allah has made known takes one out of the lawful into the unlawful, and Allah has censured with it all who depart from His acts of worship. Its origin among the people of language is ”قَدْ فَسَقَتِ الرُّطَبَةُ“ ("the fresh date has come out [fasaqat]"), when it comes out of its skin.
Were some of these nominatives accusative according to the meaning, it would be permissible outside the Qurʾān: if you said ”حُرِّمَتْ عَلى النّاسِ المَيْتَةُ والدَّمَ ولَحْمَ الخِنْزِيرِ“, construing it on the meaning "and Allah has forbidden blood and the flesh of swine", that would be permissible. But as for the Qurʾān, it is a mistake in it for us to recite with what has not been recited by one who is an exemplar in reading, because reading is a sunna (received practice) that is not to be exceeded.
His saying: ﴿اليَوْمَ يَئِسَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِن دِينِكُمْ﴾: ”اَلْيَوْمَ“ is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), and by it is not meant — and Allah knows best — one particular day.
Its meaning: now the disbelievers have despaired of your religion. This is as you say: ”أنا اليَوْمَ قَدْ كَبِرْتُ“ ("today I have grown old") and ”وهَذا الشَّأْنُ لا يَصْلُحُ في اليَوْمِ“ ("this affair is not proper today"), meaning "I, now" and "in this time". Its meaning is that Allah has turned away the fear which was about to overtake you from them today, and they have despaired of Islam's coming to nothing, and there has come to you what you were promised in His saying: ﴿لِيُظْهِرَهُ عَلى الدِّينِ كُلِّهِ﴾ [al-Tawba: 33]. ”اَلدِّينُ“ is a name for everything by which Allah has made His creation worship Him and commanded them to remain steadfast upon, and by which they are recompensed, and which He commanded them to make their habit. We have explained that at His saying: ﴿مالِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ﴾ [al-Fātiḥa: 4].
His saying: ﴿فَلا تَخْشَوْهم واخْشَوْنِ﴾, i.e. let your fear be for Allah alone, for you are now safe from any religion prevailing over Islam. And likewise — and Allah knows best — His saying: ﴿اليَوْمَ أكْمَلْتُ لَكم دِينَكُمْ﴾, i.e. now I have perfected the religion for you by sparing you the fear of your enemy and giving you victory over them; as you say: "Now dominion has become complete for us, and what we want has become complete for us, in that we have been spared the one we used to fear." It has also been said: ”اَلْيَوْمَ أكْمَلْتُ لَكم دِينَكم“, i.e. I have completed for you the obligation of what you need in your religion; and that is permissible and good. But that the religion of Allah should at any time be incomplete — no.
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ في مَخْمَصَةٍ﴾, i.e. whoever is driven by necessity in a famine, because ”اَلْمَخْمَصَةُ“ is severe emptiness of the belly. ﴿غَيْرَ مُتَجانِفٍ لإثْمٍ﴾, i.e. not inclining to sin. ﴿فَإنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾, i.e. Allah has permitted him that out of mercy from Him and as an easing for His creation. And likewise ﴿فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ غَيْرَ باغٍ ولا عادٍ﴾ [al-Baqara: 173], i.e. not eating it by way of regarding it as lawful, ”ولا عادٍ“, i.e. not exceeding the measure of need, and not eating it for pleasure. ﴿فَإنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾.

zajjaj:50-50.t:
His saying: ﴿أفَحُكْمَ الجاهِلِيَّةِ يَبْغُونَ﴾, that is: the Jews, while they are the People of the Book, seek in the judgement of the two adulterers a ruling that Allah did not command, as the people of the Jāhiliyya (pre-Islamic ignorance) do.
His saying: ﴿وَمَن أحْسَنُ مِنَ اللَّهِ حُكْمًا لِقَوْمٍ يُوقِنُونَ﴾, that is: whoever has certainty sees clearly the justice of Allah and His judgement. And "حُكْمًا" is accusative as tafsīr (tamyīz, specification).

zajjaj:51-51.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَن يَتَوَلَّهم مِنكم فَإنَّهُ مِنهُمْ﴾, that is: whoever supports them against the Muslims is one of those whom he supports.

zajjaj:52-52.t:
His saying: ﴿فَتَرى الَّذِينَ في قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ يُسارِعُونَ فِيهِمْ﴾: "اَلْمَرَضُ" (the sickness) here is hypocrisy in religion, and the meaning of "يُسارِعُونَ فِيهِمْ" is: (they hasten) in helping them against the Muslims. ﴿يَقُولُونَ نَخْشى أنْ تُصِيبَنا دائِرَةٌ﴾, that is: we fear that the matter will not be completed for the Prophet ﷺ; and the meaning of "دائِرَةٌ" is: the matter turns away from the state it is in.
His saying: ﴿فَعَسى اللَّهُ أنْ يَأْتِيَ بِالفَتْحِ﴾, that is: perhaps Allah will make the Muslims prevail; and "عَسى" (perhaps), coming from Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — is binding (certain).
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿أوْ أمْرٍ مِن عِنْدِهِ﴾, that is: or that the Prophet ﷺ be commanded to expose the affair of the hypocrites by killing them, ﴿فَيُصْبِحُوا عَلى ما أسَرُّوا في أنْفُسِهِمْ نادِمِينَ﴾.

zajjaj:53-53.t: His saying: ﴿وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أهَؤُلاءِ الَّذِينَ أقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أيْمانِهِمْ﴾, that is: the believers, whose inner and outer selves are one, say: "Are these the ones who swore, and strengthened their oaths, that they are believers, and that they are with you, your helpers against whoever opposes you?" ﴿حَبِطَتْ أعْمالُهُمْ﴾, that is: the faith they displayed has gone, and every good they did has been nullified by their disbelief and their turning away from the path of Allah, as He said: ﴿الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أضَلَّ أعْمالَهُمْ﴾ [Muḥammad: 1]. The meaning is: and those who believe will say at that time, that is, at a time in which Allah exposes their hypocrisy.

zajjaj:54-54.t:
His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَن يَرْتَدَّ مِنكم عَنْ دِينِهِ﴾: in Arabic there are three ways of saying it: "مَن يَرْتَدِدْ", "مَن يَرْتَدَّ" with fatḥa on the dāl, and "مَن يَرْتَدِّ مِنكم" with kasra on the dāl. Kasra is not permitted in recitation, because it has not been transmitted that it was read so. As for "مَن يَرْتَدِدْ", it is the original form, because when the second of the two doubled letters is made quiescent, the doubling appears (unassimilated), as in His saying: ﴿إنْ يَمْسَسْكم قَرْحٌ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 140]; and had it been read "إنْ يَمَسَّكم قَرْحٌ" it would have been correct (Arabic), but you must not recite it so, because it contradicts the Muṣḥaf, and because recitation is a followed practice (sunna). It is established from Nāfiʿ and the people of Syria (al-Shām): "يَرْتَدِدْ" with two dāls. The position of "يَرْتَدَّ" is jussive (jazm), and its original form, as we said, is "يَرْتَدِدْ"; the first dāl was assimilated into the second, and the second was given fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Abū ʿUbayd said: they disliked the combination of two voweled letters; and I reckon he erred, because the combination of two voweled letters of the same kind is too frequent in speech to be counted, as in "شَرَرٌ", "مَدَدٌ", "قِدَدٌ" and "خُدَدٌ". Kasra in His saying "مَن يَرْتَدِّ" is permissible (linguistically) because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, since it is the basic (vowel for that). The fāʾ is the answer to the condition (jazāʾ), that is: "if anyone apostatises from his religion", that is: the one which is faith.
﴿فَسَوْفَ يَأْتِي اللَّهُ بِقَوْمٍ يُحِبُّهم ويُحِبُّونَهُ﴾, that is: with a people who are believers, not hypocrites; ﴿أذِلَّةٍ عَلى المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾, that is: their side is gentle toward the believers — not that they are lowly and humiliated; ﴿أعِزَّةٍ عَلى الكافِرِينَ﴾, that is: their side is harsh toward the disbelievers.
His saying: ﴿يُجاهِدُونَ في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ ولا يَخافُونَ لَوْمَةَ لائِمٍ﴾: because the hypocrites used to watch out for the disbelievers, back them, and fear their blame; so Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known that one whose faith is sound does not fear, in supporting the religion with his hand or his tongue, the blame of any blamer. Then Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known that this only comes about through His guidance and His granting of success, and said — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿ذَلِكَ فَضْلُ اللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَن يَشاءُ﴾, that is: their love for Allah, the gentleness of their side toward the Muslims, and their severity against the disbelievers are a favour from Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — upon them; they have no success except through Him — Mighty and Majestic is He.

zajjaj:55-55.t:
His saying: ﴿إنَّما ولِيُّكُمُ اللَّهُ ورَسُولُهُ والَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾: He made clear who the believers are, saying: ﴿الَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ الصَّلاةَ﴾. Establishing it is completing it with all its obligations, and the first of its obligations is sound faith in it. This is like your saying: "So-and-so is upholding (قائِمٌ) the knowledge he has taken charge of", its interpretation being that he gives the work its full rights. The meaning of "يُقِيمُونَ" is from your saying: "This is the mainstay (قِوام) of the matter". As for His saying: ﴿أذِلَّةٍ عَلى المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 54], it is genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of "قَوْمٍ"; and if you wish it may be accusative in two ways: one of them is the ḥāl (circumstantial), in the sense of "He loves them and they love Him" in the state of their humbling themselves toward the believers and their being mighty against the disbelievers; and it may be accusative by way of praise (al-madḥ).
As for His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَقَفَّيْنا عَلى آثارِهِمْ بِعِيسى ابْنِ مَرْيَمَ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 46], that is: We sent ʿĪsā following in the footsteps of the messengers, that is: We made him follow them.
His saying: ﴿مُصَدِّقًا لِما بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مِنَ التَّوْراةِ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 46], that is: (confirming) what preceded of the Torah. "مُصَدِّقًا" is accusative as a ḥāl. It may be a description of "اَلْإنْجِيلَ", in which case it is made accusative by His saying "وَآتَيْناهُ", the meaning being: "We gave him the Gospel, there being in it guidance and light, and confirming". And it may be a ḥāl of "عِيسى", the meaning being: "We gave him the Gospel, (he being) a guide and confirming", because when it is said "We gave him the Gospel in which is guidance", the one who brought the guidance is a guide. The best is that it be in the sense of: "We sent ʿĪsā following, bringing the Gospel, guiding and confirming what was before him of the Torah"; and the proof that it is a description of "عِيسى" is His saying: ﴿يا بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ إنِّي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ إلَيْكم مُصَدِّقًا لِما بَيْنَ يَدَيَّ مِنَ التَّوْراةِ﴾ [al-Ṣaff: 6]. And His saying: ﴿لِكُلٍّ جَعَلْنا مِنكم شِرْعَةً ومِنهاجًا﴾ [al-Māʾida: 48]: some of them said: "اَلشِّرْعَةُ" is the religion and "اَلْمِنهاجُ" is the way; and it was said: "اَلشِّرْعَةُ" and "اَلْمِنهاجُ" both mean the way, and the way here is the religion; but when the wording differs, several words are brought by which the story and the matter are emphasised, as in the poet's saying:
؎حُيِّيتَ مِن طَلَلٍ تَقادَمَ عَهْدُهُ ∗∗∗ أقْوى وأقْفَرَ بَعْدَ أُمِّ الهَيْثَمِ
(May you be greeted, O ruin whose time has grown old; it has become empty and desolate after Umm al-Haytham.)
For the meaning of "أقْوى وأقْفَرَ" indicates emptiness, except that the two words are more emphatic in (expressing) emptiness than one word. Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [Translator's note: al-Mubarrad] said: "شِرْعَةً" means the beginning of the way, and "اَلْمِنهاجُ" is the continuing way. He said: when these words are repeated in such a case, it is for an increase in meaning. He said: likewise the saying of al-Ḥuṭayʾa:
؎ألا حَبَّذا هِنْدٌ وأرْضٌ بِها هِنْدُ ∗∗∗ وهِنْدٌ أتى مِن دُونِها النَّأْيُ والبُعْدُ
(How lovely is Hind and a land in which Hind is — and Hind, between whom and me came separation and distance.)
He said: "اَلنَّأْيُ" is used for everything whose distance from you is small or great, as though he says: "اَلنَّأْيُ" is separation, be it small or great; while "اَلْبُعْدُ" is only used for something far, and the meaning of "far" according to him is that whose distance of separation is great. It is as if he says of what is near to him: "it is apart (ناءٍ) from me", and likewise of what is far from him; and "اَلنَّأْيُ" according to him is separation.

zajjaj:57-57.t:
His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَتَّخِذُوا الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا دِينَكم هُزُوًا ولَعِبًا﴾: "هُزُؤًا" has several dialectal forms. If you wish, you say "هُزُؤًا" with ḍamma on the zāy and full pronunciation of the hamza, and that is the original and the best; if you wish, you say "هُزُوًا", replacing the hamza with wāw because of the ḍamma before it and because it carries fatḥa; and if you wish, you say "هُزْءًا", with sukūn on the zāy and full pronunciation of the hamza. These three forms are good and are recited. There is another form in it, but reciting it is not permitted because it was not recited: namely, to say "هُزًا", like "هُدًى". That is permissible (linguistically) when you want to lighten the hamza of "هُزْءٌ", for one who makes the zāy quiescent: to say "هُزًا", its (the hamza's) vowel being thrown onto the zāy, just as you say "I saw a خَبًا", meaning "خَبْئًا".
His saying: ﴿مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الكِتابَ مِن قَبْلِكم والكُفّارَ﴾: the accusative in it is by conjunction to His saying: ﴿لا تَتَّخِذُوا الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا دِينَكم هُزُوًا ولَعِبًا﴾, that is: and do not take the disbelievers as allies. And "والكُفّارِ أوْلِياءَ" (in the genitive) is permissible, by conjunction to "اَلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الكِتابَ", the meaning being: "from among those who were given the Book before you and from among the disbelievers, as allies".

zajjaj:59-59.t:
His saying: ﴿قُلْ يا أهْلَ الكِتابِ هَلْ تَنْقِمُونَ مِنّا﴾: one says "نَقَمْتُ عَلى الرَّجُلِ، أنْقِمُ" and "نَقِمْتُ عَلَيْهِ، أنْقَمُ"; the better is "نَقَمْتُ، أنْقِمُ", and likewise the majority in recitation: ﴿وَما نَقَمُوا مِنهم إلا أنْ يُؤْمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ العَزِيزِ الحَمِيدِ﴾ [al-Burūj: 8]. And the verse of Ibn Qays al-Ruqayyāt was recited:
؎ما نَقِمُوا مِن أُمَيَّةَ إلّا ∗∗∗ أنَّهم يَحْلُمُونَ إنْ غَضِبُوا
(They resented nothing in Umayya except that they are forbearing when they are angered.)
with fatḥa and kasra: "نَقَمُوا" and "نَقِمُوا". The meaning of "نَقَمْتُ" is: I disliked the thing intensely.
His saying: ﴿وَأنَّ أكْثَرَكم فاسِقُونَ﴾: the meaning is: do you resent in us anything but our faith and your defiance? That is: you only disliked our faith, while you know that we are upon the truth, because you have been defiant (fasaqtum) by persisting in your religion, out of your love of leadership and your earning wealth through it.
If someone says: how can a knower know that one of the religions is true and yet prefer falsehood to truth? The answer to this is that most of what we witness is like that. Among this is that a person knows that killing brings one to the Fire, and yet kills, either preferring to soothe his rage or to take wealth; and among it is that Iblīs knew that Allah would enter him into the Fire for his disobedience, yet he preferred his desire over his nearness to Allah and worked toward entering the Fire. This is a clear matter.

zajjaj:4-4.t:
His saying: ﴿يَسْألُونَكَ ماذا أُحِلَّ لَهُمْ﴾: the position of ”ما“ is nominative. If you wish, you make it alone a noun, its khabar (predicate) being ”ذا“, and ”أُحِلَّ“ is part of the ṣila (relative clause) of ”ما“ «[Translator's note: so in the source; on this analysis أُحِلَّ would be the ṣila of ذا, which stands for the relative "that which".]»; the interpretation is: "they ask you what thing has been made lawful for them". It is also permissible for ”ما“ and ”ذا“ to be a single noun, which is likewise nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); the interpretation on this view is: "they ask you what thing has been made lawful for them", and ”أُحِلَّ لَهم“ is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿قُلْ أُحِلَّ لَكُمُ الطَّيِّباتُ وما عَلَّمْتُمْ مِنَ الجَوارِحِ﴾: ”اَلطَّيِّباتُ“ are everything whose prohibition has not come in the Book or the Sunna. The utterance indicates that among what they asked about they asked about game; but mention of "the game of what you have trained" was omitted because there is evidence for it in the utterance, as He said: ﴿واسْألِ القَرْيَةَ﴾ [Yūsuf: 82], the meaning being "and ask the people of the town".
His saying: ﴿مُكَلِّبِينَ﴾, i.e. in this state (ḥāl). One says ”رَجُلٌ مُكَلِّبٌ“ and ”كَلّابٌ“, i.e. one who hunts with dogs. In this is evidence that the meat of game caught by an untrained dog is unlawful if its slaughter was not reached in time. If the sender releases the hunting dog and it hunts and kills its prey, and the hunter has mentioned the name of Allah over the game, then it is lawful, without disagreement among people about that.
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿فَكُلُوا مِمّا أمْسَكْنَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: the jurists differed about it when [the dog] eats of the game. Some of them said: it may be eaten from even if [the dog] has eaten from it. All of that is not impossible in the language, because it may hold the game when it has killed it without eating from it, and it may hold it having eaten from it. The meaning of ﴿تُعَلِّمُونَهُنَّ مِمّا عَلَّمَكُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ is: you train them to hold the game for you. If the game goes out of sight and dies, it is not "held". In the ḥadīth: ”كُلْ ما أصْمَيْتَ، ولا تَأْكُلْ ما أنْمَيْتَ“ ("eat what you killed on the spot, and do not eat what went off wounded"). The meaning of ”كُلْ ما أصْمَيْتَ“ is: if you hunt game with a dog or otherwise, and it dies while you see that it died by your hunting, that is ”ما أصْمَيْتَ“. The origin of ”اَلصَّمَيانُ“ in the language is speed and lightness; so the meaning of ”كُلْ ما أصْمَيْتَ“ is: what you killed by your hunting while you saw it hasten into death, so that you saw it and knew without doubt that it died by your hunting. The meaning of ”ما أنْمَيْتَ“ is: what went out of your sight and died without your seeing it, so that you do not know whether it died by your hunting or whether something else befell it and killed it. One says ”نَمَتِ الرَّمْيَةُ“ when the quarry goes off with the arrow in it, and ”أنْمَيْتُ الرَّمْيَةَ“ when you shot it and it went off with the arrow in it. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
فَهْوَ لا تَنْمِي رَمِيَّتُهُ ∗∗∗ مالُهُ لا عُدَّ مِن نَفَرِهْ
(His quarry never gets away [wounded] — what ails him? May he not be counted among his kin!)
And al-Ḥarith ibn Waʿla al-Shaybānī said:
قالَتْ سُلَيْمى قَدْ غَنَيْتَ فَتًى ∗∗∗ فالآنَ لا تَصْمِي ولا تَنْمِي
(Sulaymā said: you lived once as a young man; now you neither kill outright nor [even] wound so that [the quarry] gets away.)

zajjaj:5-5.t:
His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿وَطَعامُ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الكِتابَ حِلٌّ لَكم وطَعامُكم حِلٌّ لَهُمْ﴾, i.e. the slaughtered animals of the People of the Book are lawful for you. The Muslims are unanimous that the slaughtered animals of the People of the Book are lawful for the Muslims, and they differed about other foods; but slaughtered animals are among foods, so the apparent sense — and Allah knows best — is that all their food is lawful like the slaughtered animals. ﴿وَطَعامُكم حِلٌّ لَهُمْ﴾: its interpretation is: it is lawful for you to feed them; because the lawful, the unlawful and the obligations after the bond of tawḥīd are bound only upon the people of the Sharīʿa and the religion; as for the unbelievers, what is due regarding them is killing, except those of the People of the Book who pay the jizya.
His saying: ﴿والمُحْصَناتُ مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الكِتابَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ﴾, i.e. and made lawful for you are the muḥṣanāt, who are the chaste women; and it is said: the free women. And ”اَلْكِتابَ“ indicates «[Translator's note: so vocalised in the source; the sense appears to be "the Book (i.e. the Qurʾān) indicates"]» that a slave-woman who is not a believer may not be married, because of His saying: ﴿وَمَن لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ مِنكم طَوْلا أنْ يَنْكِحَ المُحْصَناتِ المُؤْمِناتِ فَمِن ما مَلَكَتْ أيْمانُكم مِن فَتَياتِكُمُ المُؤْمِناتِ واللَّهُ أعْلَمُ بِإيمانِكم بَعْضُكم مِن بَعْضٍ فانْكِحُوهُنَّ بِإذْنِ أهْلِهِنَّ وآتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ بِالمَعْرُوفِ مُحْصَناتٍ غَيْرَ مُسافِحاتٍ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 25]. ﴿إذا آتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ﴾, i.e. when you have given them the dower by way of marriage, not by way of sifāḥ, which is fornication.
His saying: ﴿وَلا مُتَّخِذِي أخْدانٍ﴾: these are female and male companions (lovers). So Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — forbade intercourse by way of fornication or by way of taking a female companion, and made it lawful by way of iḥṣān, which is marriage, according to what the body of scholars hold.
His saying: ﴿وَمَن يَكْفُرْ بِالإيمانِ فَقَدْ حَبِطَ عَمَلُهُ﴾, i.e. whoever alters anything of what Allah has made lawful and makes it unlawful, or makes lawful anything of what Allah has made unlawful, is an unbeliever by consensus, and his deeds have come to nothing, i.e. all that by which he sought nearness to Allah — exalted be His praise — has come to nothing, and [likewise] other than that.

zajjaj:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إذا قُمْتُمْ إلى الصَّلاةِ فاغْسِلُوا وُجُوهَكُمْ﴾: the meaning is: when you intend to rise for the prayer. That is permissible only because in the utterance and in usage there is evidence for the meaning of intending. Like that is the saying of Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿فَإذا قَرَأْتَ القُرْآنَ فاسْتَعِذْ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطانِ الرَّجِيمِ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 98], the meaning being: when you intend to recite the Qurʾān, seek refuge with Allah from Satan the accursed.
His saying: ﴿وَأرْجُلَكم إلى الكَعْبَيْنِ﴾: the reading is with the accusative, and it has also been read with the genitive (khafḍ); both ways are permissible in Arabic. Whoever reads with the accusative, the meaning is: "wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows, and your feet up to the ankles, and wipe your heads", by way of fronting and postponement (al-taqdīm wa-l-taʾkhīr); that is permissible with the wāw, as He — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿يا مَرْيَمُ اقْنُتِي لِرَبِّكِ واسْجُدِي وارْكَعِي مَعَ الرّاكِعِينَ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 43], the meaning being "bow and prostrate", because bowing comes before prostration. Whoever reads ”وَأرْجُلِكم“ with the genitive conjoins it to "the heads". Some said: Jibrīl came down with wiping, and the Sunna is washing. Some of the people of language said: it is genitive by proximity (jarr ʿalā al-jiwār); but genitive by proximity does not occur in the words of Allah. Rather, wiping with this delimitation in the Qurʾān is like washing, because of His saying: ﴿فاغْسِلُوا وُجُوهَكم وأيْدِيَكم إلى المَرافِقِ﴾: He mentioned the limit in washing for the hand as up to the elbows, and the hand [extends] from the fingertips to the palm «[Translator's note: so in the source; the sense seems to be that "hand" (yad) can denote the limb from the fingertips up to the shoulder, and the limit cuts it off at the elbow.]»; so He made it obligatory on us to wash part of the hand, from the fingertips to the elbow; so the elbow is cut off from what is not washed and is included in what is washed. Some of the people of language said: its meaning is "with the elbows"; but the hand includes the elbow, so had it been "wash your hands with the elbow", there would be no benefit in [mentioning] the elbows, and the whole hand would have to be washed. But when it was said ”إلى المَرافِقِ“, [the hand] was cut off in washing at the limit of the elbow. ”اَلْمِرْفَقُ“ in the language is what is beyond the ibra (the point of the elbow), and it is the place on which one leans (yurtafaqu bihi), i.e. on which one reclines on a cushion (mirfaqa) and the like. So the elbows are the limit up to which one goes in washing it, and there is no need for the interpretation "with". And since He set the limit for the leg at the ankles — and the leg (rijl) extends from the root of the thigh to the foot — it is known that washing is from the tips of the toes to the ankles. The two kaʿbs are the two protruding bones at the end of the shank where it meets the foot. Every joint of bones is a kaʿb, except that these two kaʿbs are visible on the right and left of the top of the foot; therefore there was no need to say "the two kaʿbs whose description is such-and-such". So the evidence that washing is what is obligatory for the foot, and the evidence that wiping over the foot is not permissible, is the delimitation ”إلى الكَعْبَيْنِ“, just as came in delimiting the hand to the elbows; and no delimitation came in anything regarding wiping: He said ﴿وامْسَحُوا بِرُءُوسِكُمْ﴾ without delimitation in the Qurʾān, and likewise His saying: ﴿فَلَمْ تَجِدُوا ماءً فَتَيَمَّمُوا صَعِيدًا طَيِّبًا فامْسَحُوا بِوُجُوهِكم وأيْدِيكم مِنهُ﴾. And ”وَأرْجُلِكم“ with the genitive is permissible in the sense of "and wash", because His saying "to the ankles" has indicated that, as we have described; and washing is conjoined (yunsaqu) onto wiping, as the poet said:
يا لَيْتَ بَعْلَكِ قَدْ غَدا ∗∗∗ مُتَقَلِّدًا سَيْفًا ورُمْحا
(Would that your husband had set out girt with a sword and a spear.)
The meaning is: girt with a sword and carrying a spear. And likewise another said:
عَلَفْتُها تِبْنًا وماءً بارِدا
(I fed her straw and cold water.)
The meaning is: and I gave her cold water to drink.
His saying: ﴿وَإنْ كُنْتُمْ جُنُبًا فاطَّهَّرُوا﴾: one says for the singular ”رَجُلٌ جُنُبٌ“, and ”رَجُلانِ جُنُبٌ“, ”قَوْمٌ جُنُبٌ“ and ”اِمْرَأةٌ جُنُبٌ“, just as one says ”رَجُلٌ رِضًى“ and ”قَوْمٌ رِضًى“. It is only on the interpretation of "possessors of janāba (ذَوُو أجْنُبٍ)", because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and the maṣdar stands in place of what it was annexed to. Some of the Arabs make it dual and plural and treat the maṣdar like an active participle; when ”جُنُبٌ“ is pluralised you say for men ”جُنُبُونَ“, for women ”جُنُباتٌ“, and for two ”جُنُبانِ“.
His saying: ﴿فاطَّهَّرُوا﴾: its meaning is ”فَتَطَهَّرُوا“, except that the tāʾ is assimilated into the ṭāʾ because they are from one place [of articulation]; they and the dāl are from the tip of the tongue and the roots of the upper front teeth. When the tāʾ is assimilated into the ṭāʾ, the beginning of the word drops [its vowel], so the connective alif (alif al-waṣl) is added to it, and you begin and say ”اِطَّهَّرُوا“. He — Mighty and Majestic is He — made clear in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ what the purification of the junub is, namely full washing (ghusl), saying: ﴿وَلا جُنُبًا إلا عابِرِي سَبِيلٍ حَتّى تَغْتَسِلُوا﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 43]. ”اَلْغائِطُ“ is a euphemism for the place of relieving oneself, and ”اَلْغِيطانُ“ are low-lying parts of the ground.
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿فَتَيَمَّمُوا صَعِيدًا طَيِّبًا﴾, i.e. betake yourselves to. We have explained ”اَلصَّعِيدُ“ in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ.
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿ما يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ لِيَجْعَلَ عَلَيْكم مِن حَرَجٍ﴾, i.e. any constriction. ﴿وَلَكِنْ يُرِيدُ لِيُطَهِّرَكُمْ﴾: the lām entered to make the intention clear; the meaning is: His intention is to purify you. The poet said:
أُرِيدُ لِأنْسى ذِكْرَها فَكَأنَّما ∗∗∗ تَمَثَّلُ لِي لَيْلى بِكُلِّ سَبِيلِ
(I want to forget the memory of her, yet it is as though Laylā appears before me on every path.)

zajjaj:119-119.t:
Regarding His words: ﴿قالَ اللَّهُ هَذا يَوْمُ يَنْفَعُ الصّادِقِينَ صِدْقُهُمْ﴾: it is read both with «اليوم» in the nominative (rafʿ) and with «اليوم» in the accusative (naṣb). As for whoever puts «اليوم» in the nominative, it is as the khabar (predicate): "this is the day; Allah said: the day is one in which the truthfulness of the truthful brings benefit". And whoever puts it in the accusative does so on the basis that «يوم» is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), the meaning being: "Allah said this to ʿĪsā on a day when their truthfulness benefits the truthful", i.e. "Allah said this on the Day of Resurrection". It may also be: "Allah said these things, and this which we have mentioned takes place on a day when their truthfulness benefits the truthful".

Some claimed that «يوم» is accusative because it is annexed to the verb while being in the position of a nominative, like «يومئذ», indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa in every state. According to the Basrans this is an error: they do not permit «هذا يومَ آتيك» meaning «هذا يومُ إتيانك», because «آتيك» is an imperfect verb (fiʿl muḍāriʿ, i.e. one that resembles the noun), so annexation to it does not remove the inflection from its proper course. But they do permit «ذلك يومَ نفع زيدًا صدقُه», because the past verb does not resemble [the noun], so this is annexation to something that is not fully declinable (ghayr mutamakkin) and to something that does not resemble the fully declinable.

There is a third possibility in it: «هذا يومٌ ينفعَ الصادقين», with nunation (tanwīn) of «يوم», on the implication (iḍmār) of «هذا يومٌ ينفع فيه الصادقين صدقهم», and it would then be like His words: ﴿واتَّقُوا يَوْمًا لا تَجْزِي نَفْسٌ عَنْ نَفْسٍ شَيْئًا﴾ [al-Baqara: 48]. Similar to it is the poet's saying:
؎وَما الدَّهْرُ إلّا تارَتانِ فَمِنهُما أمُوتُ ∗∗∗ وأُخْرى أبْتَغِي العَيْشَ أكْدَحُ
(Time is nothing but two turns: in one of them I die, and in the other I seek a livelihood, toiling.)
The meaning is: "of the two there is a turn in which I die".

zajjaj:60-60.t:
His saying: ﴿قُلْ هَلْ أُنَبِّئُكم بِشَرٍّ مِن ذَلِكَ مَثُوبَةً عِنْدَ اللَّهِ﴾, that is: of something worse in recompense than what you resent of our faith. "مَثُوبَةً" is accusative as tamyīz (specification).
His saying: ﴿مَن لَعَنَهُ اللَّهُ﴾: the position of "مَن" may, if you wish, be nominative, and if you wish, genitive. Whoever makes it genitive makes it a badal (substitute) of "شَرٍّ", the meaning being: "I will inform you of the one whom Allah has cursed". And "مَن" nominative is by implying "هو" (he), as though someone said: "Who is that?", and it was said: "He is the one whom Allah has cursed", just as He — exalted be His praise — said: ﴿قُلْ أفَأُنَبِّئُكم بِشَرٍّ مِن ذَلِكُمُ النّارُ﴾ [al-Ḥajj: 72], as though He said: "It is the Fire".
His saying: ﴿وَعَبَدَ الطّاغُوتَ﴾: "اَلطّاغُوتُ" is Satan, and the interpretation of "وَعَبَدَ الطّاغُوتَ" is: he obeyed him in what he made attractive to him and incited him to. It has been read "وَعَبْدَ الطّاغُوتِ", and what I choose is "وَعَبَدَ الطّاغُوتَ". It was transmitted from Ibn Masʿūd: "وَعَبَدُوا الطّاغُوتَ", and this strengthens "وَعَبَدَ الطّاغُوتَ". As for whoever said "وَعَبُدَ الطّاغُوتِ", with ḍamma on the bāʾ and the genitive in "اَلطّاغُوتِ", according to some of the people of Arabic it is not the proper way, from two aspects: one of them is that "عَبُدَ" is on the pattern "فَعُلَ", and this is not one of the plural patterns, since they explained it as "servants of the ṭāghūt"; and the second is that it would be construed as "and He made of them the عَبُدَ of the ṭāghūt". As for whoever read "وَعُبُدَ الطّاغُوتِ", it is the plural of "عَبِيدٌ", "عُبُدٌ", like "رَغِيفٌ" and "رُغُفٌ", and "سَرِيرٌ" and "سُرُرٌ"; and it would be in the sense of "and He made of them the servants (عُبُدَ) of the ṭāghūt", on the model of "I made Zayd your brother", that is: "I ascribed him to you". The justification of "وَعَبُدَ الطّاغُوتِ", with fatḥa on the ʿayn and ḍamma on the bāʾ, is that the noun is built on "فَعُلَ", as they said "عَلُمٌ زَيْدٌ" [Translator's note: so in the text], and as I say "رَجُلٌ حَذُرٌ" (a very wary man), the interpretation of "حَذُرٌ" being that he is intense in wariness; so the interpretation of "عَبُدَ" is that he reached the utmost in obedience to Satan. It is as though the word is a single word indicating plurality, as you say to a group: "Among you is the عَبُدُ of the stick", meaning "Among you are the slaves (عَبِيدُ) of the stick". After these three forms, the nominative is permissible in His saying "وَعَبُدَ الطّاغُوتِ", so one would say "وَعَبُدُ الطّاغُوتِ", and likewise "وَعُبُدُ الطّاغُوتِ" in the nominative; but you must not recite with these two forms, even though they are permissible (linguistically), because recitation is not invented according to a permissible form; the way of recitation is only to follow those who came before. So the nominative "وَعَبُدُ الطّاغُوتِ" and "وَعُبُدُ الطّاغُوتِ" is permissible in the sense of censure (al-dhamm), the meaning being: "and they are the servants of the ṭāghūt"; as though, when He said: ﴿مَن لَعَنَهُ اللَّهُ وغَضِبَ عَلَيْهِ وجَعَلَ مِنهُمُ القِرَدَةَ والخَنازِيرَ﴾, the speech indicated their following of the devils, so it was said: "and they are the servants of the ṭāghūt". And it may be a badal of "مَن" when "مَن" is nominative, as though, when it was said: "Among them is the one whom Allah cursed and was angry with", it was said: "They are the عَبُدُ of the ṭāghūt" and "the عُبُدُ of the ṭāghūt". Also permissible in (ordinary) speech is "وَعَبْدَ الطّاغُوتِ", with sukūn on the bāʾ and fatḥa on the dāl, and it would be in two ways: one of them is that it is lightened from "عَبُدَ", as one says "عَضْدٌ" for "عَضُدٌ"; and it is possible that "عَبْدَ" is a single noun indicating the genus. Likewise, in "عَبْدَ" the nominative and accusative are permissible from two aspects, as we described for "عَبُدَ"; and the accusative may be from two aspects: one of them is in the sense of "and He made of them the slave (عَبْدَ) of the ṭāghūt", and it may be accusative by way of censure, in the sense of "I mean the slave of the ṭāghūt". And in "وَعَبْدَ", "وَعَبُدَ" and "وَعُبُدَ" the genitive is permissible as a badal of "مَن", the meaning being: "Shall I inform you of the one whom Allah cursed, and of the slave of the ṭāghūt?" But recitation is not permitted with any of these forms except the three that were transmitted and which the reciters read, namely: "عَبَدَ الطّاغُوتَ", which is the best of them, then "وَعَبُدَ الطّاغُوتِ", then "وَعُبُدَ الطّاغُوتِ".
His saying: ﴿أُولَئِكَ شَرٌّ مَكانًا وأضَلُّ عَنْ سَواءِ السَّبِيلِ﴾, that is: these, whose description this is, are worse in position and further astray from the level path, that is: from the straight course of the path. "مَكانًا" is accusative as tafsīr (specification).

zajjaj:63-63.t: His saying: ﴿لَوْلا يَنْهاهُمُ الرَّبّانِيُّونَ والأحْبارُ﴾: they are their scholars and their leaders. "اَلْحَبْرُ" is the scholar, and "اَلْحِبْرُ", with kasra, is ink. So Allah made known that their leaders and their rabble share in disbelief. The meaning of ﴿لَوْلا يَنْهاهُمُ الرَّبّانِيُّونَ﴾ is: why do they not forbid them?

zajjaj:64-64.t:
Then He — Mighty and Majestic is He — told of their enormous fabrication, saying: ﴿وَقالَتِ اليَهُودُ يَدُ اللَّهِ مَغْلُولَةٌ غُلَّتْ أيْدِيهِمْ﴾, that is: they said: His hand is withheld from being generous to us, as Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿وَلا تَجْعَلْ يَدَكَ مَغْلُولَةً إلى عُنُقِكَ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 29], whose interpretation is: do not withhold it from spending. Some of them said: the meaning of "يَدُ اللَّهِ مَغْلُولَةٌ" is: His favour is held back from us; and this view is mistaken, refuted by ﴿بَلْ يَداهُ مَبْسُوطَتانِ﴾, for the meaning would then be: "rather, His two favours are outspread", while the favours of Allah are too many to be counted.
Some of them said: they said: the hand of Allah is withheld from our enemies, that is: He does not punish us [Translator's note: so in the text («لا يُعَذِّبُنا»); the context would suggest "them", i.e. the enemies]. Some of the lexicographers said: they were only answered according to the measure of their speech: just as they said "يَدُ اللَّهِ مَغْلُولَةٌ", meaning by it to accuse Allah of stinginess, so it was said: ﴿بَلْ يَداهُ مَبْسُوطَتانِ﴾, that is: He is generous, spending as He wills. The meaning of ﴿غُلَّتْ أيْدِيهِمْ﴾ is: they were made misers, so they are the most miserly of people. And it was said: "غُلَّتْ أيْدِيهِمْ" means: they were shackled in the fire of Hell.
His saying: ﴿وَلَيَزِيدَنَّ كَثِيرًا مِنهم ما أُنْـزِلَ إلَيْكَ مِن رَبِّكَ طُغْيانًا وكُفْرًا﴾, that is: whenever something of the Quran is sent down to you, they disbelieve in it, so their disbelief increases; and al-ṭughyān there is excess and disbelief.
His saying: ﴿وَألْقَيْنا بَيْنَهُمُ العَداوَةَ والبَغْضاءَ إلى يَوْمِ القِيامَةِ﴾: Allah made them differ in their religion, hating one another, as He said: ﴿تَحْسَبُهم جَمِيعًا وقُلُوبُهم شَتّى﴾ [al-Ḥashr: 14]. So Allah cast enmity among them, and it is one of the causes by which Allah took away their fortune and their might.
His saying: ﴿كُلَّما أوْقَدُوا نارًا لِلْحَرْبِ أطْفَأها اللَّهُ﴾: this is a parable, that is: whenever they gathered against the Prophet and the Muslims and prepared to fight them, Allah scattered their gathering and corrupted their mutual relations.
His saying: ﴿وَيَسْعَوْنَ في الأرْضِ فَسادًا﴾, that is: they strive to repel Islam and to erase the mention of the Prophet ﷺ from their books.

zajjaj:66-66.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ أنَّهم أقامُوا التَّوْراةَ والإنْجِيلَ﴾, that is: if they had acted upon what is in them both, and had not concealed what they knew of the mention of the Prophet ﷺ in them; ﴿وَما أُنْـزِلَ إلَيْهِمْ مِن رَبِّهِمْ﴾, and that is — and Allah knows best — the Quran; that is: if they had acted upon what is in these books of the mention of the Prophet ﷺ and made his matter manifest, ﴿لأكَلُوا مِن فَوْقِهِمْ ومِن تَحْتِ أرْجُلِهِمْ﴾. It was said that a drought had struck them, so Allah made known that had they been God-fearing He would have made their provision ample, and by this He indicated that the drought which struck them was among the things with which He punished them. The meaning of ﴿لأكَلُوا مِن فَوْقِهِمْ﴾ is: they would have eaten from the rain of the sky, ﴿وَمِن تَحْتِ أرْجُلِهِمْ﴾: from the plants of the earth. And it was said: this may be by way of (expressing) abundance, as you say: "So-and-so is in good from the top of his head to his foot". Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — has made known that piety is ampleness in provision, saying: ﴿وَلَوْ أنَّ أهْلَ الكِتابِ آمَنُوا واتَّقَوْا﴾ [al-Māʾida: 65], and saying: ﴿وَمَن يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ مَخْرَجًا﴾ [al-Ṭalāq: 2] ﴿وَيَرْزُقْهُ مِن حَيْثُ لا يَحْتَسِبُ﴾ [al-Ṭalāq: 3], and saying in the story of Nūḥ: ﴿اسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكم إنَّهُ كانَ غَفّارًا﴾ [Nūḥ: 10] ﴿يُرْسِلِ السَّماءَ عَلَيْكم مِدْرارًا﴾ [Nūḥ: 11] ﴿وَيُمْدِدْكم بِأمْوالٍ وبَنِينَ ويَجْعَلْ لَكم جَنّاتٍ﴾ [Nūḥ: 12] — and these are orchards; so Allah promised them the most complete wealth in return for faith and seeking forgiveness.
His saying: ﴿مِنهم أُمَّةٌ مُقْتَصِدَةٌ﴾, that is: from among the People of the Book. Some of them said: by this is meant those of them who believed; and it was said: by it is meant a group who did not show the Prophet ﷺ hostility as these did. What I think — and Allah knows best — is that Allah does not call anyone who is upon anything of disbelief "moderate" (مُقْتَصِدًا). ﴿وَكَثِيرٌ مِنهم ساءَ ما يَعْمَلُونَ﴾: the meaning is: how evil a thing is their deeds.

zajjaj:67-67.t: His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها الرَّسُولُ بَلِّغْ ما أُنْـزِلَ إلَيْكَ مِن رَبِّكَ وإنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلْ فَما بَلَّغْتَ رِسالَتَهُ﴾: it is also read "رِسالاتِهِ". The meaning is: convey all that has been sent down to you from your Lord, and if you leave out anything of it you have not conveyed; that is: do not be wary of anyone, and do not leave out anything of it out of fear that something hateful may befall you. ﴿واللَّهُ يَعْصِمُكَ مِنَ النّاسِ﴾, that is: He will come between them and any harm from them reaching you. So Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — made known to him that he would be safe from them, and in this is a clear sign for the Prophet ﷺ.

zajjaj:69-69.t:
His saying: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا والَّذِينَ هادُوا والصّابِئُونَ والنَّصارى مَن آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ واليَوْمِ الآخِرِ وعَمِلَ صالِحًا فَلا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ ولا هم يَحْزَنُونَ﴾: the people of Arabic differed in explaining the nominative of "اَلصّابِئُونَ". Some of them said: the accusative governance of "إنَّ" is weak, so "اَلصّابِئُونَ" was conjoined to "اَلَّذِينَ", because their (the names') original case is the nominative; this is the view of al-Kisāʾī. Al-Farrāʾ said the like of that, except that he mentioned that this is permissible in conjunction with something like "اَلَّذِينَ" and with a pronoun — "إنِّي وزِيدٌ قائِمانِ" (I and Zayd are standing) is permissible — and that he does not permit "إنَّ زَيْدًا وعَمْرٌو قائِمانِ". This explanation is a grave audacity against the Book of Allah. That is because they claimed that the accusative governance of "إنَّ" is weak, since it only changes the noun and does not change the khabar (predicate); and this is an error, because "إنَّ" exerts two governances, the accusative and the nominative, and in Arabic there is no governor of the accusative without a nominative accompanying it, since every accusative is likened to the object, and an object does not exist without an agent, except in what has no named agent (the passive). And how can the accusative governance of "إنَّ" be weak when it steps over adverbial phrases and puts what follows them in the accusative, as in His saying: ﴿إنَّ فِيها قَوْمًا جَبّارِينَ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 22]? The accusative of inna is among the strongest of accusatives. Sībawayh, al-Khalīl and all the Basrans said: His saying ﴿والصّابِئُونَ﴾ is construed as deferred (in order) and is nominative by being the mubtadaʾ (subject); the meaning is: "Indeed those who believe and those who are Jews — whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day and does righteous deeds, no fear shall be upon them — and the Sabians and the Christians are likewise too", that is: "whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, no fear shall be upon them". And they recited in support of this the poet's saying:
؎وَإلّا فاعْلَمُوا أنّا وأنْتُمْ ∗∗∗ بُغاةٌ ما بَقِينا في شِقاقِ
(Otherwise, know that we — and you — are rebels as long as we remain in discord.)
The meaning is: "Otherwise, know that we are rebels as long as we remain in discord, and you are likewise too". Sībawayh claimed that some of the Arabs err and say: "إنَّهم أجْمَعُونَ ذاهِبُونَ" (they all are going) and "إنَّكَ وزَيْدٌ ذاهِبانِ" (you and Zayd are going); Sībawayh made this an error and made it like the poet's saying:
؎بَدا لِيَ أنِّي لَسْتُ مُدْرِكَ ما مَضى ∗∗∗ ولا سابِقٌ شَيْئًا إذا كانَ جائِيا
(It has become clear to me that I cannot overtake what has passed, nor outstrip anything when it is coming.)
As for "مَن آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ", when He has (already) mentioned "اَلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا": by "اَلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا" here He means only the hypocrites who displayed faith with their tongues; and what indicates that this is the meaning here is what preceded in His saying: ﴿لا يَحْزُنْكَ الَّذِينَ يُسارِعُونَ في الكُفْرِ مِنَ الَّذِينَ قالُوا آمَنّا بِأفْواهِهِمْ ولَمْ تُؤْمِن قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 41]. The meaning of "اَلصّابِئُ" is: one who goes out of the body of the religions, because they do not follow the scriptures. The Arabs say: "قَدْ صَبَأ نابُ البَعِيرِ" (the camel's canine has come out) and "صَبَأ سِنُّ الصَّبِيِّ" (the child's tooth has come out), when it emerges. As for their saying "ضَبَأتْ", with the dotted ḍād, its meaning is: it hid in the ground, and from it the name "ضابِئٌ" is derived. Al-Kisāʾī said: "اَلصّابِئُونَ" is conjoined to what is in "هادُوا" (its pronoun), as though He said: "they became Jews, they and the Sabians". This view is mistaken from two aspects: one of them is that (it would mean) the Sabian shares with the Jew in Judaism [Translator's note: the text reads «أنَّ الصّابِئَ يُشارِكُ اليَهُودِيَّ في اليَهُودِيَّةِ»; the objection is evidently that this view would make the Sabian share in Judaism]; and if he mentions that "هادُوا" means "they repented", this too is a mistake in this place, because the meaning of "اَلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا" here is only faith with their mouths, since by it the hypocrites are meant. Do you not see that He said: "whoever believes in Allah"? Had they been believers, there would have been no need to say: "if they believe, they have their reward".

zajjaj:70-70.t: His saying: ﴿فَرِيقًا كَذَّبُوا وفَرِيقًا يَقْتُلُونَ﴾: the meaning is: whenever a messenger came to them, they belied one party and killed another party. As for belying, the Jews and the Christians share in it; as for killing, it was the Jews specifically — not the Christians — who used to kill the prophets. The messengers were of two kinds: messengers who brought laws and scriptures, such as Mūsā, ʿĪsā, Ibrāhīm and Muḥammad — may Allah bless them and grant them peace — and these were protected from the creation; no one was able to kill any one of them; and messengers who came with commanding the right and forbidding the wrong and urging adherence to the religion, such as Yaḥyā and Zakariyyā — may Allah bless them both and grant them peace.

zajjaj:71-71.t: His saying: ﴿وَحَسِبُوا ألا تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ﴾: it is read "ألّا تَكُونَ" with the accusative and "ألّا تَكُونُ" with the nominative. Whoever reads with the nominative, the meaning is: "that there will be no trial (فِتْنَةٌ)", that is: "they reckoned their deeds would not bring trial upon them"; that is because they used to say that they were the sons of Allah and His beloved ones. ﴿فَعَمُوا وصَمُّوا﴾: this is a parable, its interpretation being that they did not act upon what they heard nor upon what they saw of the signs, so they became like the blind and the deaf. Then Allah turned to them in forgiveness, that is: He sent Muḥammad ﷺ to them to teach them that Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — had turned to them in forgiveness if they believed and affirmed the truth; but most of them did not believe, so He — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿ثُمَّ عَمُوا وصَمُّوا كَثِيرٌ مِنهُمْ﴾, that is: after the matter had become clearer to them through the Prophet — upon him be peace. ﴿كَثِيرٌ مِنهُمْ﴾ is nominative from three aspects. One of them is that it is a badal (substitute) of the wāw (the pronoun), as though, when He said ﴿عَمُوا وصَمُّوا﴾, He substituted "many of them" for it, that is: "many of them became blind and deaf", as you say: "جاءَنِي قَوْمُكَ أكْثَرُهم" (your people came to me, most of them). And it is possible that the verb was given plural form while preceding (its agent), as the lexicographers related: "أكَلُونِي البَراغِيثُ" (the fleas ate me). And the proper way is that "كَثِيرٌ مِنهم" be the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), the meaning being: "Those of blindness and deafness are many of them".

zajjaj:8-8.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿قَوّامِينَ لِلَّهِ شُهَداءَ بِالقِسْطِ﴾, i.e. with justice.
”شُهَداءَ“, i.e. making clear the religion of Allah, because the witness makes clear what he bears witness to.
His saying: ﴿وَلا يَجْرِمَنَّكم شَنَآنُ قَوْمٍ عَلى ألا تَعْدِلُوا﴾: ”شَنَآنُ قَوْمٍ“ means the hatred of a people, i.e. let not your hatred of the polytheists induce you to abandon justice. Whoever says ”شَنْآنُ قَوْمٍ“, its meaning is [likewise] the hatred of a people. One says ”أجْرَمَنِي كَذا وكَذا“, ”جَرَمَنِي“, ”جَرَّمَنِي“ and ”أُجْرِمْتُ“ with one meaning. And it has been said: ”لا يَجْرِمَنَّكم“ means: let it not bring you into crime (jurm), as you say ”آثَمْتُهُ“, i.e. I brought him into sin.

zajjaj:9-9.t: His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ﴾: this is the completion of the utterance. One says ”وَعَدْتُ الرَّجُلَ“, meaning "I promised him good", and ”أوْعَدْتُ الرَّجُلَ“, meaning "I threatened him with evil". When you mention the thing promised, you say in both cases ”واعَدْتُهُ“ «[Translator's note: so in the source; the usual statement is that with the thing mentioned one says وَعَدْتُهُ for both good and evil.]», and when you do not mention the thing promised you say for good ”وَعَدْتُهُ“ and for evil ”أوْعَدْتُهُ“. So He — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ﴾, which indicated good; then He made that good clear, saying: ﴿لَهم مَغْفِرَةٌ﴾, i.e. a covering over their sins, ﴿وَأجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾, a recompense for their faith.

zajjaj:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكم إذْ هَمَّ قَوْمٌ أنْ يَبْسُطُوا إلَيْكم أيْدِيَهم فَكَفَّ أيْدِيَهم عَنْكُمْ﴾: it is related in the exegesis that Banū Qurayẓa and Banū al-Naḍīr had made a covenant with the Prophet ﷺ to abandon fighting, and that he would help them with their blood-monies and they would help him with the blood-monies of the Muslims. Two men from the Muslims were killed, and the Prophet ﷺ spoke to them about their blood-monies; they promised him a time at which he would come to them. So the Prophet went, he and Abū Bakr, ʿUmar and ʿAlī. When they reached them, they resolved on treachery and on killing the Prophet ﷺ and those with him. So Allah revealed to him and informed him of what they had resolved, and they left the place where they were. The Jews told them that their pots were boiling, and he ﷺ informed them that revelation had come down to him about what they had resolved. This is among the signs that indicate his prophethood. It is also said that this refers back to His saying: ﴿اليَوْمَ يَئِسَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِن دِينِكُمْ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 3], i.e. you have been given victory over them; so He said: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكم إذْ هَمَّ قَوْمٌ أنْ يَبْسُطُوا إلَيْكم أيْدِيَهم فَكَفَّ أيْدِيَهم عَنْكُمْ﴾. Both views — and Allah knows best — are permissible, because Allah — exalted be His praise — has made Islam prevail over all other religions.

zajjaj:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أخَذَ اللَّهُ مِيثاقَ بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ﴾, i.e. Allah took from them the covenant upon His oneness and belief in His messengers. ﴿وَبَعَثْنا مِنهُمُ اثْنَيْ عَشَرَ نَقِيبًا﴾: ”اَلنَّقِيبُ“ in the language is like the commander and the guarantor; we shall make clear its true sense and derivation, if Allah wills. One says ”نَقَبَ الرَّجُلُ عَلى القَوْمِ، يَنْقُبُ“ when he becomes a naqīb over them; and "the man was not a naqīb, but now he has become one (naquba)", and his office is al-niqāba. Likewise ”عَرَفَ عَلَيْهِمْ“ when he becomes an ʿarīf (overseer), "and now he has become one". The first sign of mange that appears is called ”اَلنُّقْبَةُ“, plural ”اَلنُّقُبُ“. The poet said:
مُتَبَذِّلًا تَبْدُو مَحاسِنُهُ ∗∗∗ يَضَعُ الهِناءَ مَواضِعَ النُّقْبِ
(In working clothes, his fine qualities showing, he puts the tar exactly on the spots of mange.)
And ”اَلنُّقْبَةُ“, plural ”نُقُبٌ“, is a pair of trousers a woman wears without legs. One says: ”فُلانَةٌ حَسَنَةُ النُّقْبَةِ، والنِّقابِ“ ("so-and-so has a fine niqba and veil"). One says: ”في فُلانٍ مَناقِبُ جَمِيلَةٌ“ ("so-and-so has fine virtues"), and ”هو حَسَنُ النَّقِيبَةِ“, i.e. of good character. One says ”كَلْبٌ نَقِيبٌ“: it is that the dog's larynx is pierced so that its voice is not raised in barking; only the misers among the Arabs did that, so that a guest would not come knocking upon hearing the dogs bark. This whole section is united by [the idea of] an effect that has depth and penetration. Of that is ”نَقَبْتُ الحائِطَ“, i.e. I reached the far end in piercing it; and of that is al-nuqba from mange, because it is a disease that penetrates deeply — the evidence for that is that the camel is smeared with tar and the taste of the tar is found in its flesh. And ”اَلنُّقْبَةُ“ is these legless trousers, which are made very open and pierced. And the woman's niqāb is what shows of her face-veiling: the eyes and the eye-sockets. And ”اَلنَّقَبُ“ and ”النُّقْبُ“ are a road through a mountain. He was called ”نَقِيبٌ“ only because he knows the inner state of the people's affairs and knows their virtues (manāqib), and he is the way to knowing their affairs.
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَعَزَّرْتُمُوهُمْ﴾: Abū ʿUbayda said: ”عَزَّرْتُمُوهم“ means "you honoured them". Others said: ”عَزَّرْتُمُوهم“ means "you supported them", and this is the truth — and Allah knows best. That is because ”اَلْعَزْرُ“ in the language is repelling, and the interpretation of ”عَزَّرْتُ فُلانًا“ is: I disciplined him, I did to him what deters him from wrongdoing; just as ”نَكَّلْتُ بِهِ“ means I did to him what must make him shrink from repeating it. So the interpretation of ”عَزَّرْتُمُوهم“ is: you supported them by repelling their enemies from them. Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿وَتُعَزِّرُوهُ وتُوَقِّرُوهُ﴾ [al-Fatḥ: 9]. So if taʿzīr were the same as tawqīr (revering), then the better [reading] in the language would be seeking help and support when it is due, and honouring is included in it «[Translator's note: the sentence is so in the source and its wording appears disturbed; the intended argument is that taʿzīr in that verse cannot simply mean tawqīr, since tawqīr is mentioned separately, and that support already includes honouring.]»; because supporting the prophets is defending them, protecting their blood, honouring them and revering them.
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿فَقَدْ ضَلَّ سَواءَ السَّبِيلِ﴾, i.e. he has strayed from the straight course of the way.

zajjaj:13-13.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿فَبِما نَقْضِهِمْ مِيثاقَهُمْ﴾: ”ما“ is void (laghw); the meaning is "so for their breaking their covenant". The meaning of ”ما“ that is void in governing (al-mulghāh fī al-ʿamal) is emphasis of the account. ﴿لَعَنّاهُمْ﴾, i.e. We distanced them from mercy. ﴿وَجَعَلْنا قُلُوبَهم قاسِيَةً﴾, i.e. dry. One says of the merciful man: ”لَيِّنُ القَلْبِ“ ("soft of heart"), and of the man who is not merciful: ”قاسِي القَلْبِ، ويابِسُ القَلْبِ“ ("hard of heart, dry of heart"). ”اَلْقاسِي“ in the language, and ”اَلْقاسِحُ“ with ḥāʾ, mean the extremely hard.
His saying: ﴿يُحَرِّفُونَ الكَلِمَ عَنْ مَواضِعِهِ﴾: ”اَلْكَلِمُ“ is the plural of ”كَلِمَةٌ“, and the interpretation of ”يُحَرِّفُونَ“ is: they change it to other than what was sent down.
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَنَسُوا حَظًّا مِمّا ذُكِّرُوا بِهِ﴾: the meaning of ”نَسُوا“ is: they abandoned a portion of what they were reminded of.
His saying: ﴿وَلا تَزالُ تَطَّلِعُ عَلى خائِنَةٍ مِنهُمْ﴾: ”خائِنَةٍ“ has the meaning of ”خِيانَةٍ“ (treachery); the meaning is: you will not cease to discover treachery from them. The pattern ”فاعِلَةٌ“ is frequent among the nouns of maṣdars, such as ”عافاهُ اللَّهُ، عافِيَةً“ and His saying: ﴿فَأُهْلِكُوا بِالطّاغِيَةِ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 5]. One may also say ”رَجُلٌ خائِنَةٌ“ ("a very treacherous man"). The poet said:
حَدَّثْتَ نَفْسَكَ بِالوَفاءِ ولَمْ تَكُنْ ∗∗∗ لِلْغَدْرِ خائِنَةً مُغِلَّ الإصْبَعِ
(You told yourself to be faithful, and you were not, in treachery, a thorough betrayer, slipping your finger [into the spoils].)
He said ”خائِنَةً“ by way of intensification (mubālagha), because he is addressing a man. He says: do not carry off [goods] and slip your finger into the goods, putting it in for betrayal; and ”مُغِلَّ يَدِكَ مِن خائِنَةٍ“. It is also possible — and Allah knows best — that ”عَلى خائِنَةٍ“ means "on a treacherous group (عَلى فِرْقَةٍ خائِنَةٍ)".
His saying: ﴿إلا قَلِيلا مِنهُمْ﴾: accusative by exception.

zajjaj:14-14.t: His saying: ﴿فَأغْرَيْنا بَيْنَهُمُ العَداوَةَ والبَغْضاءَ إلى يَوْمِ القِيامَةِ﴾: by it are meant the Christians. By His saying ”أغْرَيْنا“ is meant: We made that cling to them. One says ”غَرَّيْتُ بِالرَّجُلِ غَرًى“, with a short final alif (maqṣūr), when I cling to him; this is the view of al-Aṣmaʿī. Someone other than al-Aṣmaʿī said: ”غَرِيتُ بِهِ غَراءً“; and it is the glue (al-ghirāʾ) with which things are glued, by which things are made to stick. The interpretation of ”أغْرَيْنا بَيْنَهُمُ العَداوَةَ والبَغْضاءَ“ is that they became sects, some declaring others unbelievers: among them the Nestorians, the Jacobites and the Melkites — who are the Byzantines (al-Rūm); each sect of them is hostile to the other.

zajjaj:15-15.t: His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿قَدْ جاءَكم مِنَ اللَّهِ نُورٌ وكِتابٌ مُبِينٌ﴾: the light is Muḥammad ﷺ. Guidance, or light, is what makes things clear and shows the eyes their reality; so the likeness of what the Prophet ﷺ brought into hearts, in its making clear and its dispelling of darkness, is like the likeness of light.

zajjaj:16-16.t: ﴿يَهْدِي بِهِ اللَّهُ مَنِ اتَّبَعَ رِضْوانَهُ﴾: and ”رُضْوانَهُ“ — [it is said] with kasra and ḍamma. ﴿سُبُلَ السَّلامِ﴾: plural of ”سَبِيلٌ“; ”اَلسُّبُلُ“ are the ways. So it is possible — and Allah knows best — that it means "the ways of salām", i.e. the ways of safety (salāma), by which whoever possesses them is safe in his religion; and it is possible — and Allah knows best — that ”سُبُلَ السَّلامِ“ means the ways of Allah, ”اَلسَّلامُ“ (al-Salām) being one of the names of Allah.

zajjaj:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿عَلى فَتْرَةٍ مِنَ الرُّسُلِ﴾, i.e. after an interruption, because the Prophet ﷺ was sent after an interruption of the messengers; for the messengers, up to the time when ʿĪsā was raised, came tatrā, i.e. in succession, one coming after another.
His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿أنْ تَقُولُوا ما جاءَنا مِن بَشِيرٍ﴾: some said its meaning is "lest you say (ألّا تَقُولُوا): no bearer of good tidings came to us", i.e. Allah sent the Prophet ﷺ so that you would not say: no bearer of good tidings came to us. Like it is His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكم أنْ تَضِلُّوا﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 176], meaning ”ألّا تَضِلُّوا“. Others said: ”أنْ تَقُولُوا“ means ”كَراهَةَ أنْ تَقُولُوا“ ("out of aversion that you should say"), and ”كَراهَةَ“ was omitted, as He — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿واسْألِ القَرْيَةَ﴾ [Yūsuf: 82], meaning "ask the people of the town". We have explained this exhaustively at the end of Sūrat al-Nisāʾ.

zajjaj:20-20.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَجَعَلَكم مُلُوكًا﴾: it is like "He made you possess your own affairs, with no overpowering one overpowering you in them". Some said: He made you people with dwellings into which none enters upon you except with permission; and the meaning goes back to possessing one's affairs.
His saying: ﴿وَآتاكم ما لَمْ يُؤْتِ أحَدًا مِنَ العالَمِينَ﴾: it is that Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — sent down upon them the manna and the quails, and shaded them with the clouds.

zajjaj:21-21.t: His saying: ﴿ادْخُلُوا الأرْضَ المُقَدَّسَةَ الَّتِي كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ﴾: ”اَلْمُقَدَّسَةَ“ means the purified. It is said in the exegesis that it is Damascus, Palestine and part of Jordan. And Bayt al-Maqdis was named ”اَلْمَقْدِسِ“ only because ”اَلْمَقْدِسُ“ is the place in which one purifies oneself; so its interpretation is: the House that purifies a person from faults. From this it is said ”اَلْقُدْسُ“, i.e. that by which one is purified, just as ”مَطْهَرَةٌ“ is said of what one performs ablution from; it is only the pattern ”مَفْعَلَةٌ“ from ”اَلطُّهْرُ“ (purity).

zajjaj:22-22.t: His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿قالُوا يا مُوسى إنَّ فِيها قَوْمًا جَبّارِينَ﴾: the interpretation of ”اَلْجَبّارُ مِنَ الآدَمِيِّينَ“ ("the jabbār among humans") is: the insolent tyrant who compels people to what he wants. And Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — is al-Jabbār, al-ʿAzīz, the One who is beyond being made to slip; Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — commands what He wills; there is none to repel His command and none to revise His judgment. They described them only with power, arrogance and invincibility. ”قَوْمًا“ is accusative by ”إنَّ“, ”جَبّارِينَ“ is its naʿt (adjective), and the khabar (predicate) is His saying ”فِيها“.

zajjaj:23-23.t: His saying: ﴿قالَ رَجُلانِ مِنَ الَّذِينَ يَخافُونَ أنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِما﴾, i.e. Allah had favoured them both with faith. ﴿ادْخُلُوا عَلَيْهِمُ البابَ﴾: it is as though they both knew that if that gate were entered, victory would come about.

zajjaj:24-24.t:
His saying: ﴿قالُوا يا مُوسى إنّا لَنْ نَدْخُلَها أبَدًا ما دامُوا فِيها﴾, i.e. we do not accept counsel about entering it, nor a command, while these tyrants are in it. So Allah — exalted be His praise — made known that these People of the Book did not accept [guidance] from the prophets before the Prophet ﷺ, and that opposition is their way. In this information is evidence establishing the prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ, because he informed them of what is known only from reading a book, or from report, or from revelation; and the Prophet's ﷺ upbringing is known to have been devoid of any mention of the stories of the Children of Israel, and such that he did not read their books; so nothing remained as the source of knowing that except revelation.
His saying: ﴿فاذْهَبْ أنْتَ ورَبُّكَ فَقاتِلا﴾: the speech of the Arabs is ”اِذْهَبْ أنْتَ وزَيْدٌ“, and the grammarians consider ”اِذْهَبْ وزَيْدٌ“ ugly, because an overt noun is not conjoined to a [latent] pronoun; the pronoun intended (in the mind) has no sign, so the noun would become conjoined to what is connected to the verb and inseparable from it. As for His saying: ﴿فَأجْمِعُوا أمْرَكم وشُرَكاءَكُمْ﴾ [Yūnus: 71], for whoever reads it with the nominative, that is permissible only because the object strengthens the utterance — and likewise ”ضَرَبْتُ زَيْدًا وعَمْرٌو“ — just as the entry of ”لا“ strengthens the utterance; Allah — exalted be His praise — said: ﴿لَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ ما أشْرَكْنا ولا آباؤُنا﴾ [al-Anʿām: 148].

zajjaj:25-25.t:
His saying: ﴿قالَ رَبِّ إنِّي لا أمْلِكُ إلا نَفْسِي وأخِي﴾: ”أخِي“ is in the nominative position, and it may be in the accusative position. The meaning is: he said, "My Lord (رَبِّي), I have power over none but myself", and my brother likewise has power over none but himself. «[Translator's note: the source paraphrase writes رَبِّي; the verse has رَبِّ.]» Its nominative is from two angles. One of them is that it is conjoined (nasaq) to the position of ”إنِّي“; the meaning: I have power over none but myself, and my brother likewise. Like it is His saying: ﴿أنَّ اللَّهَ بَرِيءٌ مِنَ المُشْرِكِينَ ورَسُولُهُ﴾ [al-Tawba: 3]. And it is possible that it is conjoined to ”ما“ «[Translator's note: so in the source; what is meant is apparently the latent subject pronoun]» in His saying ”أمْلِكُ“; so the meaning is: I — I and my brother — have power over none but ourselves. And it is possible for ”أخِي“ to be in the accusative position from two angles. One of them is that it is conjoined to the yāʾ in ”إنِّي“; the meaning: I and my brother have power over none but ourselves — "I have power over none but myself, and my brother has power over none but himself". And it is possible that it is conjoined to ”نَفْسِي“, so the meaning is: "I have power over none but myself, and I have power over none but my brother", because his brother, if obedient to him, is in the possession of his obedience.
His saying: ﴿إذْ جَعَلَ فِيكم أنْبِياءَ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 20]: ”أنْبِياءَ“ is not declined (lā yuṣraf, i.e. it is a diptote) because it is built on the alif of the feminine, and it is undeclined both as definite and indefinite because it contains the sign of the feminine; and that [alif], in addition to being the sign of the feminine, is built into the noun, without the feminine being formed off a masculine, as with ”قائِمٌ“ and ”قائِمَةٌ“.

zajjaj:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿فَإنَّها مُحَرَّمَةٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً يَتِيهُونَ في الأرْضِ﴾: it means that entering the Holy Land is forbidden to them, i.e. they are prevented from that. Some grammarians said: ”أرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً“ may be accusative by His saying ”مُحَرَّمَةٌ“, and may be accusative by His saying ”يَتِيهُونَ“. As for its being accusative by ”مُحَرَّمَةٌ“, that is a mistake, because the exegesis has come stating that it is forbidden to them forever; so ”أرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً“ is accusative by His saying ”يَتِيهُونَ“. It is said: Allah punished them by their remaining in the wilderness (al-tīh) for forty years, wandering, with no resting place to settle them, until the adults who had disobeyed Allah died, the young grew up, and those were born who were not included among them in the disobedience. It is said that Mūsā and Hārūn were with them in the wilderness; some said Mūsā and Hārūn were not in the wilderness, because the wilderness was a punishment and prophets are not punished. It is possible that they were both in the wilderness and that Allah — exalted be His name — made that easy for them, as He made the fire easy for Ibrāhīm and made it coolness and safety for him, though its nature is to burn.
His saying: ﴿فَلا تَأْسَ عَلى القَوْمِ الفاسِقِينَ﴾: it is possible that this is an address to Mūsā, and possible that it is an address to Muḥammad ﷺ, i.e. do not grieve over a people whose way has never ceased to be disobedience and opposition to the messengers.

zajjaj:73-73.t:
His saying: ﴿لَقَدْ كَفَرَ الَّذِينَ قالُوا إنَّ اللَّهَ ثالِثُ ثَلاثَةٍ﴾: its meaning is that they said: "Allah is one of three gods", or: "one out of three gods". Only the genitive is permissible in "ثَلاثَةٍ", because the meaning is "one of three". But if you say "زَيْدٌ ثالِثُ اثْنَيْنِ" (Zayd is the third of two) or "رابِعُ ثَلاثَةٍ" (the fourth of three), both the genitive and the accusative are permissible.
