The accusative is according to your saying: "The people were three, and he made them four", and "I will be their fourth (رابِعُهم) tomorrow" or "the one making the three four (رابِعُ الثَّلاثَةِ) tomorrow"; and whoever uses the genitive does so by dropping the tanwīn (nunation), as He — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿هَدْيًا بالِغَ الكَعْبَةِ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 95].
His saying: ﴿وَما مِن إلَهٍ إلا إلَهٌ واحِدٌ﴾: "مِن" has come in as emphatic, and the meaning is: "There is no god except One God".
His saying: ﴿وَإنْ لَمْ يَنْتَهُوا عَمّا يَقُولُونَ لَيَمَسَّنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنهم عَذابٌ ألِيمٌ﴾: the meaning of "اَلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنهم" is: those who persisted in this religion and this saying.

zajjaj:75-75.t:
His saying: ﴿إلا رَسُولٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهِ الرُّسُلُ﴾, that is: his healing of the one born blind and the leper, and his bringing of miraculous signs, are not because he is a god; he only brought signs as Mūsā brought signs and as Ibrāhīm brought signs. ﴿وَأُمُّهُ صِدِّيقَةٌ﴾, that is: intense in truthfulness and in affirming the truth. "صِدِّيقَةٌ" was applied to her only because He sent Jibrīl to her, and Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿وَصَدَّقَتْ بِكَلِماتِ رَبِّها وكُتُبِهِ﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 12]. "صِدِّيقٌ" is "فِعِّيلٌ", one of the intensive patterns, as you say: "فُلانٌ سِكِّيتٌ" (so-and-so is very silent), that is: intense in silence.
His saying: ﴿كانا يَأْكُلانِ الطَّعامَ﴾: this is a clear argument, that is: they both live only by nourishment, as the rest of the children of Adam live; so how can one be a god whom nothing sustains except the eating of food?! His saying: ﴿انْظُرْ كَيْفَ نُبَيِّنُ لَهُمُ الآياتِ﴾, that is: the clear signs; ﴿ثُمَّ انْظُرْ﴾, that is: look, after the clarification, ﴿أنّى يُؤْفَكُونَ﴾, that is: from where are they turned away from the clear truth. Of everything that you turned away from something and overturned from it, you say: "أفَكْتُهُ آفِكُهُ إفْكًا". And "اَلْإفْكُ" is lying; it was only so named because it is a turning away from the truth. And "اَلْمُؤْتَفِكاتُ" are the winds that come from (various) directions without one single course.

zajjaj:77-77.t: His saying: ﴿وَلا تَتَّبِعُوا أهْواءَ قَوْمٍ قَدْ ضَلُّوا مِن قَبْلُ﴾: "أهْواءَ" is the plural of "هَوًى", and "هَوى النَّفْسِ" (the soul's desire) is maqṣūr (ending in short alif), because it is like "اَلْفَرَقُ", and "فَعَلٌ" has its plural as "أفْعالٌ". Its interpretation is: do not follow their lusts, because they preferred lusts to clear explanation and proof. Whatever mention there is in the Quran of following desire is blameworthy, as in His saying: ﴿وَلا تَتَّبِعِ الهَوى فَيُضِلَّكَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ [Ṣād: 26], His saying: ﴿واتَّبَعَ هَواهُ فَتَرْدى﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 16], and His saying: ﴿وَما يَنْطِقُ عَنِ الهَوى﴾ [al-Najm: 3]. And the meaning of ﴿وَأضَلُّوا كَثِيرًا﴾ is: the many followed them; ﴿وَضَلُّوا عَنْ سَواءِ السَّبِيلِ﴾, that is: by their misleading (others) they strayed from the straight course of the path.

zajjaj:78-78.t:
His saying: ﴿لُعِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِن بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ﴾: the interpretation of "لُعِنُوا" (they were cursed) is: they were removed far from the mercy of Allah. ﴿عَلى لِسانِ داوُدَ وعِيسى ابْنِ مَرْيَمَ﴾: it has come in the tafsīr (exegetical tradition) that some people gathered upon an abomination, and Dāwūd — upon him be peace — came to them to forbid them from it; he asked permission to enter upon them, and they said: "We are apes, and we do not understand what you say." So he said: "Be apes!" and Allah transformed them into apes. And (it came) that some people gathered against ʿĪsā, reviling him concerning his mother and stoning him, so he asked Allah to make them swine, and they became swine. That is their being cursed on the tongue of Dāwūd and ʿĪsā. And it is possible that Dāwūd and ʿĪsā were informed that Muḥammad ﷺ is a prophet, and that they cursed whoever would disbelieve in him.
His saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِما عَصَوْا وكانُوا يَعْتَدُونَ﴾, that is: that cursing was due to their disobedience and their transgression. In "ذَلِكَ", the kāf is for address, and the lām in "ذَلِكَ" was given kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. The Kufans did not mention the kasra of this lām in any of their books, nor did they know it; and this is among the things they ought to have spoken about, since "ذَلِكَ" is a pointing to everything that is remote from you. However, their leaving off speaking is more beneficial to them than their speaking, since the first thing they uttered regarding "فَعِلَ" contradicted the rest of Arabic grammar, and we have explained that long ago.

zajjaj:79-79.t: His saying: ﴿لَبِئْسَ ما كانُوا يَفْعَلُونَ﴾, that is: how evil, as an evil thing, their doing is. The lām came in for the oath and emphasis. We have explained why it was given fatḥa, and (likewise) the rest of the particles that occurred — meaning why they were given fatḥa or kasra — and the Kufans did not explain anything of that.

zajjaj:80-80.t: His saying: ﴿أنْ سَخِطَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: "أنْ" may be accusative, on the interpretation: "Evil is that thing, because (لِأنْ) Allah was displeased with them", that is: "because it earned them displeasure". And "أنْ" may be in the position of the nominative by implying "هو" (it), as though it were said: "It is that Allah was displeased with them", as you say: "نِعْمَ الرَّجُلُ زَيْدٌ" (how excellent a man is Zayd).

zajjaj:82-82.t:
His saying: ﴿لَتَجِدَنَّ أشَدَّ النّاسِ عَداوَةً لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اليَهُودَ والَّذِينَ أشْرَكُوا﴾: that is because the Jews backed the idolaters against the believers, while the believers believe in Mūsā and the Torah that he brought; they ought to have been closer to those who agreed with them in faith in their prophet and their book, yet they backed the idolaters out of envy of the Prophet ﷺ.
His saying "لَتَجِدَنَّ": this lām is the lām of the oath, and the nūn has come in to distinguish between the present and the future. This is the doctrine of al-Khalīl, Sībawayh and those whose knowledge is trusted.
His saying "عَداوَةً" is accusative as tamyīz (specification).
﴿وَلَتَجِدَنَّ أقْرَبَهم مَوَدَّةً لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا الَّذِينَ قالُوا إنّا نَصارى﴾: there is more than one view on this. It has come in the tafsīr that thirty-odd Abyssinians from among the Christians came, with a group along with them, and accepted Islam when the Prophet ﷺ recited the Quran to them. And it is possible that by it the Christians (in general) are meant, because they were less supportive of the idolaters than the Jews; and His saying ﴿وَإذا سَمِعُوا ما أُنْـزِلَ إلى الرَّسُولِ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 83] would be in that sense. ﴿بِأنَّ مِنهم قِسِّيسِينَ ورُهْبانًا﴾: and among them are people who, when they hear what has been sent down to the Messenger — by it are meant here the believers among them. "اَلْقُسُّ" and "اَلْقِسِّيسُ" are among the leaders of the Christians; as for "اَلْقَسُّ" in the language, it is talebearing and spreading talk; one says: "قَسَّ فُلانٌ الحَدِيثَ قَسًّا" (so-and-so spread the talk). The meaning of ﴿فاكْتُبْنا مَعَ الشّاهِدِينَ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 83] is: with those of Your prophets — upon them be peace — and of the believers among Your servants who have borne witness that there is no god but You.

zajjaj:84-84.t: His saying: ﴿وَما لَنا لا نُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ﴾: the position of "لا نُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ" is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: what is (the matter) with us, abandoning faith?! That is: in the state of our abandoning faith. That is because their people rebuked them for their faith, so they answered them by saying: "ما لَنا لا نُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ" (why should we not believe in Allah?).

zajjaj:86-86.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿والَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وكَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا أُولَئِكَ أصْحابُ الجَحِيمِ﴾: "اَلْجَحِيمُ" is the fire of intense blaze. "قَدْ جَحِمَ فُلانٌ النّارَ" is said when he intensifies its blaze; the lion's eye is called "جَحْمَةٌ" because of the intensity of its blazing; and the blaze of war — which is the intensity of fighting in it — is called "جاحِمٌ". The poet said:
؎والخَيْلُ لا يَبْقى لِجاحِمِها التَّخَيُّلُ والمَراحُ
؎إلّا الفَتى الصَّبّارُ في النَّجْداتِ والفَرَسُ الوَقاحُ
(And the cavalry: before its blazing heat, swagger and high spirits do not endure — except the young man steadfast in hardships and the hard-hoofed horse.)

zajjaj:87-87.t: His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تُحَرِّمُوا طَيِّباتِ ما أحَلَّ اللَّهُ لَكم ولا تَعْتَدُوا﴾: it was said that this was revealed because a group of the Companions of the Prophet had resolved to reject the world, avoid good things and castrate themselves. So Allah made known that the law of His Prophet — upon him be peace — is otherwise, and that good things should not be avoided at all. Castration was called "transgression" (اِعْتِداء), so He — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿وَلا تَعْتَدُوا﴾, that is: do not castrate yourselves, for that is transgression.

zajjaj:89-89.t:
His saying: ﴿لا يُؤاخِذُكُمُ اللَّهُ بِاللَّغْوِ﴾: "اَللَّغْوُ" in the speech of the Arabs is what is discarded and upon which no matter is bound; and what is not counted — even if it exists — is called "لَغْوًا". The poet said:
؎أوْ مِائَةً تَجْعَلُ أوْلادَها ∗∗∗ لَغْوًا وعُرْضُ المِائَةِ الجَلْمَدُ
(Or a hundred (she-camels) that make their young of no count, and the breadth of the hundred is (like) the solid rock.)
That which faces it is (like) the strength of solid rock. By that he means she-camels; he is saying: "a hundred that do not make their young part of their number". Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known that the oath for which the servant is held accountable, and for some of which expiation is obligatory, is that which proceeded upon a binding resolve. The meaning of ﴿فَكَفّارَتُهُ إطْعامُ عَشَرَةِ مَساكِينَ﴾ is: the expiation of the accountability for it, when he breaks it, is to feed ten poor persons; whether they are males, or females and males, that suffices him; but the masculine wording occurred because it is the predominant one in speech. As for the meaning of ﴿مِن أوْسَطِ ما تُطْعِمُونَ أهْلِيكُمْ﴾, some said: its most just (middle), as He — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْناكم أُمَّةً وسَطًا﴾ [al-Baqara: 143], that is: just. And "the average of what you feed your families" is of two kinds: one of them is its average in amount and value, and the other is its average in satiation: the food is not such that one goes to excess in eating it, eating beyond moderation and the measure of need, nor is it less than what suffices against hunger. ﴿أوْ كِسْوَتُهُمْ﴾: clothing is to clothe them with something like a waist-wrapper and a turban, or what resembles that. ﴿أوْ تَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ﴾: so the one who swore is given the choice of one of these three, and the best of them with Allah is the one of most benefit and best received by the poor or by the freed slave. If the people are in drought, unable to obtain food except with greater strain than clothing or freeing, then feeding is better, because the sustenance of life depends on it; otherwise freeing or clothing is better. ﴿فَمَن لَمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيامُ ثَلاثَةِ أيّامٍ﴾, that is: whoever is unable to do any of what is specified in the expiation must fast three days. "صِيامُ ثَلاثَةِ" is nominative as the mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is "كَفّارَتُهُ" [Translator's note: i.e. an implied "his expiation"], or (in the sense of) "فَكَفّارَتُهُ صِيامُ ثَلاثَةِ أيّامٍ" (then his expiation is fasting three days). And "فَصِيامٌ ثَلاثَةَ أيّامٍ" is permissible (linguistically), as He — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿أوْ إطْعامٌ في يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ﴾ [al-Balad: 14], and "أوْ عَدْلٌ ذَلِكَ صِيامًا". ﴿ذَلِكَ كَفّارَةُ أيْمانِكم إذا حَلَفْتُمْ﴾, that is: that is what covers over your sins. One says "كَفَرْتُ الشَّيْءَ" when you have covered it; and from it is His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿أعْجَبَ الكُفّارَ نَباتُهُ﴾ [al-Ḥadīd: 20], "اَلْكُفّارُ" being those who cover the seed and tend it; and the disbeliever (اَلْكافِرُ) was only called "كافِرًا" because by his disbelief he has covered over faith.

zajjaj:27-27.t: His saying: ﴿واتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأ ابْنَيْ آدَمَ بِالحَقِّ إذْ قَرَّبا قُرْبانًا﴾: it is said they were two men of the Children of Israel, because the offering used to be consumed by fire in the time of the Children of Israel; and like that is His saying: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ عَهِدَ إلَيْنا ألا نُؤْمِنَ لِرَسُولٍ حَتّى يَأْتِيَنا بِقُرْبانٍ تَأْكُلُهُ النّارُ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 183]. And it is said: they were Ādam's own two sons, one of them ”هابِيلُ“ (Hābīl) and the other ”قابِيلُ“ (Qābīl). They offered an offering, ﴿فَتُقُبِّلَ مِن أحَدِهِما ولَمْ يُتَقَبَّلْ مِنَ الآخَرِ﴾. When a man offered an offering he would prostrate, and fire would come down and consume his offering; that was the sign of the offering's acceptance. The fire came down and consumed Hābīl's offering and did not consume Qābīl's offering, so Qābīl envied him and threatened him with killing, saying: ﴿لأقْتُلَنَّكَ قالَ إنَّما يَتَقَبَّلُ اللَّهُ مِنَ المُتَّقِينَ﴾. The meaning is: the one from whom it was not accepted said: "I will surely kill you"; mention of "the one from whom it was not accepted" was omitted because there is evidence for it in the utterance. Like that in ordinary speech: ”إذا رَأيْتَ الحاكِمَ والمَظْلُومَ كُنْتَ مَعَهُ“ ("when you see the judge and the wronged one, you are with him"), the meaning being: you are with the wronged one. It is said that the sword was forbidden at that time, as it was when the Prophet ﷺ was in Makka, and as it was forbidden in the time of ʿĪsā; so he said:

zajjaj:28-28.t: ﴿لَئِنْ بَسَطْتَ إلَيَّ يَدَكَ لِتَقْتُلَنِي ما أنا بِباسِطٍ يَدِيَ إلَيْكَ﴾, i.e. I will not requite you, nor fight you, nor kill you. ﴿إنِّي أخافُ اللَّهَ رَبَّ العالَمِينَ﴾

zajjaj:29-29.t: ﴿إنِّي أُرِيدُ أنْ تَبُوءَ بِإثْمِي وإثْمِكَ﴾, i.e. that you return to Allah with my sin and your sin. ﴿فَتَكُونَ مِن أصْحابِ النّارِ﴾. The meaning of ”بِإثْمِي“ is: with the sin of killing me; ”وَإثْمِكَ“: [your sin] because of which your offering was not accepted. I.e. if you kill me, I want that. ﴿وَذَلِكَ جَزاءُ الظّالِمِينَ﴾

zajjaj:30-30.t:
﴿فَطَوَّعَتْ لَهُ نَفْسُهُ﴾: [his soul] went along with him. Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd al-Mubarrad said: ”فَطَوَّعَتْ لَهُ نَفْسُهُ“ is the pattern ”فَعَّلَتْ“ from ”اَلطَّوْعُ“ (compliance). The Arabs say: ”طاعَ لِهَذِهِ الظَّبْيَةِ أُصُولُ هَذِهِ الشَّجَرَةِ“ ("the roots of this tree yielded themselves to this gazelle"), and ”طاعَ لَهُ كَذا وكَذا“, i.e. it came to him willingly.
His saying: ﴿فَأصْبَحَ مِنَ الخاسِرِينَ﴾, i.e. of those who lost their good deeds. When he killed him, he stripped him of his clothes and left him naked in the desolate land.

zajjaj:31-31.t: ﴿فَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ غُرابًا يَبْحَثُ في الأرْضِ﴾: some said: Allah sent a crow scratching [the earth] over another, dead crow, ﴿لِيُرِيَهُ كَيْفَ يُوارِي سَوْءَةَ أخِيهِ﴾. And it is said: rather, Allah honoured him [the slain brother] by sending a crow which scattered dust over him, to show him how to cover. ﴿قالَ يا ويْلَتا أعَجَزْتُ أنْ أكُونَ مِثْلَ هَذا الغُرابِ﴾: one says ”عَجَزْتُ عَنِ الأمْرِ، أعْجِزُ، عَجْزًا، ومُعْجَزَةً، ومَعْجِزَةً“. As for ”يا ويْلَتى“, the pause on it outside the Qurʾān is ”يا ويْلَتاهُ“. Vocatives addressed to non-humans, such as ﴿يا حَسْرَةً عَلى العِبادِ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 30], ﴿يا ويْلَتى أألِدُ وأنا عَجُوزٌ﴾ [Hūd: 72] and ﴿قالَ يا ويْلَتا أعَجَزْتُ﴾, occur in the speech of the Arabs only to alert those addressed, and [to say] that the time for which these things are called is their [proper] time. So the meaning is: "O my woe, come, for this is your season, for woe has befallen me"; and likewise ”يا عَجَبًا“, the meaning being: "O wonder, this is your time". On this pattern is the speech of the Arabs.

zajjaj:32-32.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأصْبَحَ مِنَ النّادِمِينَ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 31] ﴿مِن أجْلِ ذَلِكَ﴾: the best is that it be [construed as] ﴿مِن أجْلِ ذَلِكَ كَتَبْنا عَلى بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ﴾. One says ”أجَلْتُ الشَّيْءَ، أأْجِلُهُ، أجَلًا“ when I have brought it about (committed it). Khawwāt ibn Jubayr said:
وَأهْلِ خِباءٍ صالِحٍ كُنْتُ بَيْنَهم ∗∗∗ قَدِ احْتَرَبُوا في عاجِلٍ أنا آجِلُهُ
(And many a family of a goodly tent, I was among them; they fell to fighting over a sudden matter which I had brought about.)
i.e. I am the one who caused it. As for the interpretation of ”اَلْوَيْلُ“ in the language: Sībawayh said: ”اَلْوَيْلُ“ is a word said at the time of perdition. And it is said: ”اَلْوَيْلُ“ is a valley in Hell; this does not depart from the views of the people of language, because whoever falls into that has fallen into perdition.
His saying: ﴿أنَّهُ مَن قَتَلَ نَفْسًا بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ أوْ فَسادٍ في الأرْضِ﴾: ”فَسادٍ“ is conjoined to ”نَفْسٍ“; the meaning is "without corruption (بِغَيْرِ فَسادٍ)". ﴿فَكَأنَّما قَتَلَ النّاسَ جَمِيعًا﴾, i.e. all the believers are the adversaries of the killer, and he has wronged them as one would who set out to kill them all. ﴿وَمَن أحْياها فَكَأنَّما أحْيا النّاسَ جَمِيعًا﴾, i.e. whoever rescues it from drowning, or burning, or a collapse, or whatever would kill without doubt, or rescues it from misguidance, it is as though he had given life to all people, i.e. his reward with Allah is the reward of one who gave life to them all. And it is possible that, in conferring a kindness on them by giving life to their believing brother, he is in the position of one who gave life to every single one of them.
If someone says: how can his reward be the reward of one who gave life to them all? The answer to this is like the answer regarding His saying — Exalted is He —: ﴿مَن جاءَ بِالحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أمْثالِها﴾ [al-Anʿām: 160]: the interpretation is that the reward which, if assigned to the good deed, would be the utmost one could wish for — the doer of it is given ten times that.

zajjaj:33-33.t:
His saying: ﴿إنَّما جَزاءُ الَّذِينَ يُحارِبُونَ اللَّهَ ورَسُولَهُ ويَسْعَوْنَ في الأرْضِ فَسادًا أنْ يُقَتَّلُوا﴾: the position of ”أنْ“ is nominative; the meaning is: their recompense is only killing, or crucifixion, or cutting off the hands and feet on opposite sides; because when a speaker says "your recompense is only a dinar", the meaning is "your recompense is nothing but a dinar". The view of the scholars is that this verse was revealed concerning the unbelievers specifically. It is related in the exegesis that Abū Barza al-Aslamī had made a covenant with the Prophet ﷺ that he would not molest with harm anyone heading for the Prophet ﷺ and would not be prevented from that, and that the Prophet ﷺ would not prevent anyone heading for Abū Barza. A group heading for the Prophet passed by Abū Barza, and his companions attacked them, killed and took property. So Allah — Exalted is He — sent down [revelation] to His Prophet: Jibrīl came to him and informed him that Allah commanded him that whoever of them he caught who had killed and taken property, he should kill and crucify; whoever had killed and not taken property, he should kill; and whoever had taken property and not killed, he should cut off his hand for taking the property and cut off his foot for terrorising the road. Some said: the Muslims have the choice in the matter of the polytheists: if they wish they kill them and crucify them, or cut off their hands and feet on opposite sides. As for the meaning of ﴿يُنْفَوْا مِنَ الأرْضِ﴾, there are two views on it. Some said: whoever kills him, his blood is unavenged (hadar), i.e. his killer is not held liable for his blood. And it is said: ”أوْ يُنْفَوْا مِنَ الأرْضِ“ means that they are fought wherever they turn in it, and are not left to flee. One says ”نَفَيْتُ الشَّيْءَ أنْفِيهِ، نَفْيًا، ونُفايَةً“; and ”اَلنُّفايَةُ“ is what is thrown away and rejected, the scanty remainder, like ”اَلْبُرايَةُ“ (shavings) and ”اَلنُّحاتَةُ“ (chippings).
His saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ لَهم خِزْيٌ في الدُّنْيا﴾: one says ”خَزِيَ الرَّجُلُ، يَخْزى، خِزْيًا“ when he is disgraced and bewildered with shame; and ”قَدْ خَزى، يَخْزِي، خِزايَةً“ when he is ashamed, as if he is perplexed at doing something ugly. «[Translator's note: so vocalised in the source; the usual form for "to be ashamed" is خَزِيَ يَخْزى خَزايَةً.]»

zajjaj:90-90.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿إنَّما الخَمْرُ والمَيْسِرُ والأنْصابُ والأزْلامُ رِجْسٌ مِن عَمَلِ الشَّيْطانِ﴾: al-khamr (wine) is well known; it is whatever clouds (خامَرَ) the mind, and we have explained it. "اَلْمَيْسِرُ" is gambling, all of it. Its origin is that it was gambling over a slaughter-camel: they used to divide the slaughter-camel — according to the view of al-Aṣmaʿī — into twenty-eight portions, and according to the view of Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī into ten portions; and Abū ʿUbayda said: I do not know the number of portions. They used to cast lots over them with qidāḥ, which are wooden arrows that have names — we will explain them as they really are in our book, if Allah wills — and each man obtains from that gambling according to his means. This is the origin of al-maysir, and all gambling is like al-maysir. We have explained al-anṣāb and al-azlām at the beginning of the sūra. So Allah made known that gambling, wine, seeking to divide by divining arrows, and the worship of idols are rijs (filth). "اَلرِّجْسُ" in the language is a name for every deed that is regarded as foul; so Allah went to the utmost in condemning these things, called them rijs, and made known that Satan makes that attractive to the children of Adam. One says: "رَجِسَ الرَّجُلُ، يَرْجَسُ" and "رَجَسَ يَرْجُسُ" when he does an ugly deed. And "اَلرَّجْسُ", with fatḥa on the rāʾ, is intensity of sound; so it is as though "اَلرِّجْسُ" is the deed whose mention is ugly and which rises high in ugliness. One says "سَحابٌ ورَعْدٌ رَجّاسٌ" (loud-rumbling cloud and thunder) when it is intense in sound. The poet said:
؎وَكُلُّ رَجّاسٍ يَسُوقَ الرُّجَّسا
(And every loud-rumbling (cloud) driving the loud-rumbling ones.)
As for "اَلرِّجْزُ" with zāy, it is punishment, or the deed that leads to punishment. Allah said: ﴿لَئِنْ كَشَفْتَ عَنّا الرِّجْزَ لَنُؤْمِنَنَّ لَكَ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 134], that is: (if) you remove the punishment from us.
And His saying: ﴿والرُّجْزَ فاهْجُرْ﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 5]: they said: (it is) the worship of idols. The origin of "اَلرِّجْزُ" in the language is the succession of movements; from that is their saying "رَجْزاءُ" (of a she-camel) when her legs tremble as she rises; and from this is "رَجَزُ الشِّعْرِ" (the rajaz metre of poetry), because it has the shortest verses of poetry, and the passage in it from one verse to the next is quick, as in his saying:
؎يا لَيْتَنِي فِيها جَذَعْ ∗∗∗ أخُبُّ فِيها وأضَعْ
(Would that I were a young man in it, trotting and hastening in it.)
and as in their saying:
؎صَبْرًا بَنِي عَبْدِ الدّارِ
(Steadfastness, O sons of ʿAbd al-Dār!)
and as in their saying:
؎ما هاجَ أحْزانًا وشَجْوًا قَدْ شَجا
(What stirred up sorrows and a grief that has grieved.)
Al-Khalīl claimed that rajaz is not poetry, but is only half-verses or third-verses. Al-Khalīl's proof for that is what was transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ: «سَتُبْدِي لَكَ الأيّامُ ما كُنْتَ جاهِلًا، وتَأْتِيكَ مَن لَمْ تُزَوَّدْ بِالأخْبارِ» (The days will reveal to you what you did not know, and the one you did not provision will bring you the news). Al-Khalīl said: had a half-verse been poetry, «سَتُبْدِي لَكَ الأيّامُ ما كُنْتَ جاهِلًا» would not have run on the tongue of the Prophet ﷺ; and the second half came in a form other than the composition of poetry, because a half-verse is not called "poetry" nor "a verse"; and if it were permissible to call a half-verse "poetry", a (metrical) foot of it would be called "poetry". And there ran on the tongue of the Prophet ﷺ, in what was transmitted: «أنا النَّبِيُّ لا كَذِبْ، أنا ابْنُ عَبْدِ المُطَّلِبْ» (I am the Prophet, no lie; I am the son of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib). Some of them said: it is only "لا كَذِبَ أنا ابْنُ عَبْدِ المُطَّلِبِ", with fatḥa on the bāʾ, by continuous reading. Al-Khalīl said: had it been poetry, it would not have run on the tongue of the Prophet ﷺ; Allah said: ﴿وَما عَلَّمْناهُ الشِّعْرَ وما يَنْبَغِي لَهُ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 69], that is: it does not come easily to him. Al-Akhfash said: al-Khalīl's view was that these things are poetry, and I say that they are not poetry; and he mentioned that he bound al-Khalīl (by argument) to (the view) that al-Khalīl (then) adopted [Translator's note: so in the text; this contradicts the attribution to al-Khalīl just above — al-Akhfash apparently means that al-Khalīl earlier held rajaz to be poetry, and that al-Akhfash's argument led him to adopt the opposite view]. The meaning of "اَلرِّجْزُ" is: the punishment that shakes violently with a violent, successive shaking because of its intensity. The meaning of ﴿فاجْتَنِبُوهُ﴾ is: leave it.
Its derivation in the language is: be to one side (جانِبًا) of it, that is: in a corner apart.

zajjaj:94-94.t: His saying: ﴿لَيَبْلُوَنَّكُمُ اللَّهُ بِشَيْءٍ مِنَ الصَّيْدِ تَنالُهُ أيْدِيكم ورِماحُكُمْ﴾: this lām is the lām of the oath, and the lām [Translator's note: so in the text; the context of "meeting of two quiescents" and «اُغْزُوَنَّ» suggests the wāw is meant] has fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, as in some people's saying: "اُغْزُوَنَّ يا رَجُلُ" (go raiding, O man!). As for the lām of "لَتُبْلَوُنَّ", Sībawayh claimed that it is indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, and we have thoroughly explained this before this place. The meaning of "لَيَبْلُونَّكم" is: He will surely test your obedience against your disobedience, ﴿بِشَيْءٍ مِنَ الصَّيْدِ﴾. He — Mighty and Majestic is He — said ﴿بِشَيْءٍ مِنَ الصَّيْدِ﴾ and so made it partitive, and this bears two interpretations: one of them is that it refers to land game to the exclusion of sea game; and the second is that since He meant the game (forbidden) as long as they are in iḥrām, that was part of the game. And it may be in a third way, this "مِن" being explicative of one genus among genera; you say: "I will surely test you with something of silver (الوَرِقِ)", that is: "I will test you with the genus that is silver", as He — exalted be His praise — said: ﴿فاجْتَنِبُوا الرِّجْسَ مِنَ الأوْثانِ﴾ [al-Ḥajj: 30], while idols are all filth; the meaning is: avoid the filth which is idols. The meaning of His saying ﴿تَنالُهُ أيْدِيكم ورِماحُكُمْ﴾: that which hands reach is such as ostrich eggs and its chicks, and whatever is small and rises from its resting place, other than ostriches; and (spears reach) the rest of what escapes the hand by its movement, of all other wild animals. So He forbade all land game — locusts and everything that is hunted; its hunting is forbidden as long as they are in the state of iḥrām. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made clear that everything hunted in the Sanctuary (al-Ḥaram) is forbidden, whether they are in iḥrām or not in iḥrām.

zajjaj:95-95.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَن قَتَلَهُ مِنكم مُتَعَمِّدًا﴾, that is: intending to kill it, as though he forgets that he is in iḥrām while intending the killing; and it is possible that he intends the killing while knowing that he is in iḥrām.
His saying: ﴿فَجَزاءٌ مِثْلُ ما قَتَلَ مِنَ النَّعَمِ﴾ and "فَجَزاءُ مِثْلِ ما قَتَلَ", with "مِثْلُ" in the nominative and the genitive. Whoever puts both in the nominative does so in the sense of "then upon him is a recompense like that which he killed", so "مِثْلُ" is a naʿt (adjective) of the recompense; or "جَزاءٌ" may be nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) and "مِثْلُ قَتْلِ" [Translator's note: so in the text] the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, the meaning being: "then the recompense of that act is the like of what he killed". And whoever uses the genitive means: "then upon him is a recompense of the like of that killed (animal) from the livestock (النَّعَمِ)". "اَلنَّعَمُ" in the language is camels, cattle and sheep; if camels are alone among them they are called "نَعَمٌ", but if sheep and cattle are alone they are not called "نَعَمًا". So for a wild ass and a wild cow, he owes a sacrificial camel (بَدَنَةٌ), and for gazelles, a sheep from the flock.
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿يَحْكُمُ بِهِ ذَوا عَدْلٍ مِنكُمْ﴾, that is: from the people of your religion. So the one who killed the game must ask two upright jurists about the recompense of what he killed, and they say to him: "Have you killed game before this while in iḥrām?" If he admits that he killed game before that, they do not judge anything against him, because of the saying of Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَمَن عادَ فَيَنْتَقِمُ اللَّهُ مِنهُ﴾. If he does not admit it, they look into what he killed: if it is like camels, they judge camels against him, ﴿هَدْيًا بالِغَ الكَعْبَةِ﴾; if it is like sheep, they judge the like of that against him; and if the value does not reach (that), they examine and estimate its value, and he feeds the poor with its price, each poor person — some said — a ṣāʿ of wheat, and some said half a ṣāʿ; or he fasts the equivalent of that, according to what the Sunna requires. And it is possible — and this is the better (reading) in the language — that "أوْ" is for choice: if he wishes he offers a sacrificial animal, and if he wishes they estimate the value of the offering for him and he feeds (the poor) in its place as we described, or makes the like of that in fasting, because "أوْ" is for choice. Some said: it is as though, if he cannot afford camels or sheep, he should feed or fast. What the wording requires is choice, and the jurists know best the Sunna in that; but I choose, according to the doctrine of language, that he has the choice.
His saying: ﴿هَدْيًا بالِغَ الكَعْبَةِ﴾ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: they judge it, it being determined that it be offered. "بالِغَ الكَعْبَةِ": its wording is the wording of a definite, but its meaning is indefinite; the meaning is "بالِغًا الكَعْبَةَ" (reaching the Kaʿba), except that the tanwīn (nunation) was dropped for lightness. The meaning of His saying ﴿أوْ عَدْلُ ذَلِكَ﴾ is: or the like of that. Some said: "عِدْلُ الشَّيْءِ" is its like of its own kind, and "عَدْلُهُ", with fatḥa on the ʿayn, is its like not of its kind; and he said: except that some of the Arabs err and make "اَلْعَدْلُ" and "اَلْعِدْلُ" mean "the like", even if it is not of the kind of the first. The Basrans said: "اَلْعَدْلَ" and "اَلْعِدْلُ" mean "the like", the meaning being one, whether for a like of the same kind or not of the kind, just as "the like" — whether it is of the kind of the thing or not of its kind — is (called) "مِثْلٌ"; and they did not say that the Arabs erred. It is not the case that when someone makes a mistake it obliges you to say that some of the Arabs erred.
His saying ﴿صِيامًا﴾ is accusative as tamyīz (specification); the meaning is: or the like of that in fasting, that he may taste the evil consequence (وَبال) of his deed. "اَلْوَبالُ" is the heaviness of something in what is disliked; from it is their saying "طَعامٌ وبِيلٌ" and "ماءٌ وبِيلٌ" (unwholesome food, unwholesome water), when they are heavy and not conducive to growth in livestock. He — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿فَأخَذْناهُ أخْذًا وبِيلا﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 16], that is: heavy and severe. And "اَلْوَبِيلُ" is the fuller's beating-stick, and from this it is called "وَبِيلٌ". Ṭarafa ibn al-ʿAbd said:
؎عَقِيلَةُ شَيْخٍ كالوَبِيلِ يَلنْدَدِ
(The prized one of an old man like a fuller's stick, fiercely contentious.)
His saying: ﴿وَمَن عادَ فَيَنْتَقِمُ اللَّهُ مِنهُ﴾: the fāʾ is the answer to the condition, and the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "whoever returns, deeming the game lawful after Allah has forbidden it to him, Allah will take vengeance on him", that is: Allah will punish him. And it may be: "whoever returns, making light of the command of Allah, his recompense is punishment, like the recompense of one who kills a soul".

zajjaj:96-96.t: His saying: ﴿وَطَعامُهُ مَتاعًا لَكم ولِلسَّيّارَةِ﴾, that is: the game of the sea has been made lawful for you, and the food of the sea has been made lawful for you for the travellers. As for its game, it is well known; as for its food, there has been disagreement about it. Some said: what the water has receded from, and which is taken without hunting, is its food. And he said: its food is everything that the water has watered and caused to grow — that is the food of the sea, because it grew from the water of the sea. So Allah made known to them that what has been made lawful for them is abundant on land and sea, and that what has been forbidden to them is only the game of the land in the state of iḥrām. And the Prophet ﷺ instituted the prohibition of hunting in the Sanctuary, so that He would have left them without excuse regarding the vengeance upon whoever returns to what Allah has forbidden him, despite the abundance of what Allah has made lawful for him. "مَتاعًا" is accusative, an emphatic maṣdar (verbal noun), because when He said "أُحِلَّ لَكم" it was an indication that He had given them enjoyment of it; just as, when He said: ﴿حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكم أُمَّهاتُكُمْ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 23], it was an indication that He had prescribed that for them, so He said: ﴿كِتابَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 24].

zajjaj:97-97.t:
His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿جَعَلَ اللَّهُ الكَعْبَةَ البَيْتَ الحَرامَ قِيامًا لِلنّاسِ﴾: it was said that it was named "اَلْكَعْبَةَ" only because of the squareness of its top. The meaning of "قِيامًا لِلنّاسِ" is: among what they were commanded to undertake (يَقُومُوا) by way of obligation in it; and likewise: ﴿والشَّهْرَ الحَرامَ والهَدْيَ والقَلائِدَ﴾. As for whoever said that it is security, that is because Allah said: ﴿وَمَن دَخَلَهُ كانَ آمِنًا﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 97]; and the Arabs always used to leave off fighting in the sacred month, and it was called "Rajab the Deaf" (رَجَبَ الأصَمَّ), because the sound of weapons was not heard in it. As for whoever said: "These things were made so that people would undertake them", he only meant their acts of devotion in the Ḥajj and its means.
His saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ لِتَعْلَمُوا أنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ ما في السَّماواتِ وما في الأرْضِ﴾: there are two views on it. One of them is that when Allah made the Sacred Land secure from fear, while people used to kill one another, and made the sacred month one in which killing is refrained from, while the people were people of the Jāhiliyya, He showed by that that He knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, since in the times of greatest corruption He established that by which security is obtained. There is another view on it, and to me it is clearer: that this refers back to what Allah announced on the tongue of His Prophet in this sūra, in His saying: ﴿مِنَ الَّذِينَ قالُوا آمَنّا بِأفْواهِهِمْ ولَمْ تُؤْمِن قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 41]. So He told of their hypocrisy which had been hidden from the Muslims, and of what He told — that they are listeners to lies, listeners for other people who have not come to you. So Allah exposed what they had kept secret regarding the story of the two adulterers, and their asking him ﷺ, and what we have explained of their conduct in that; so Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — made His Prophet and the believers aware of everything they had concealed from them.
So the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: that is so that you may know the unseen which I have told you of from Allah; it indicates to you that He knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth. The proof of this view is His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿ما عَلى الرَّسُولِ إلا البَلاغُ واللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ ما تُبْدُونَ وما تَكْتُمُونَ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 99].

zajjaj:34-34.t: His saying: ﴿إلا الَّذِينَ تابُوا مِن قَبْلِ أنْ تَقْدِرُوا عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: it is possible that the position of ”اَلَّذِينَ“ is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being ﴿فاعْلَمُوا أنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾, the meaning being "Forgiving, Merciful to them"; the meaning is: but those who repent before you gain power over them — Allah is Forgiving, Merciful to them. And it is possible, in ﴿إلا الَّذِينَ تابُوا مِن قَبْلِ أنْ تَقْدِرُوا عَلَيْهِمْ﴾, that the position of ”اَلَّذِينَ“ is accusative, so the meaning would be: "their recompense is what we have described, except those who repent"; then He said afterwards: ﴿أنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾. Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — has made repentance for you «[Translator's note: so in the source (لَكَ); the context suggests "for them", i.e. for the unbelievers who repent]», so ward off from them the ḥadd punishments that became due on them in their unbelief, so that this may be a greater inducement to enter Islam. And He made the repentance of believers from fornication, killing and theft not lift from them the carrying out of the ḥadd punishments upon them, while it averts from them punishment in the Hereafter; because in carrying out the ḥadd punishments there is well-being for the believers, and life. Allah — exalted be His praise — said: ﴿وَلَكم في القِصاصِ حَياةٌ يا أُولِي الألْبابِ﴾ [al-Baqara: 179].

zajjaj:35-35.t: His saying: ﴿وابْتَغُوا إلَيْهِ الوَسِيلَةَ﴾: its meaning is: seek nearness to Him. ﴿وَجاهِدُوا في سَبِيلِهِ لَعَلَّكم تُفْلِحُونَ﴾, i.e. that you may triumph over your enemy. ”اَلْمُفْلِحُ“ is the one who attains that in which lies the utmost soundness of his state.

zajjaj:38-38.t:
His saying: ﴿والسّارِقُ والسّارِقَةُ فاقْطَعُوا أيْدِيَهُما﴾: the grammarians differed in explaining the nominative in them. Sībawayh and many of the Basrans said: this, and His saying: ﴿الزّانِيَةُ والزّانِي فاجْلِدُوا كُلَّ واحِدٍ مِنهُما مِائَةَ جَلْدَةٍ﴾ [al-Nūr: 2], and His saying: ﴿واللَّذانِ يَأْتِيانِها مِنكم فَآذُوهُما﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 16] — these things are in the nominative on the meaning: "and among what Allah has prescribed for you: the male thief and the female thief, the fornicatress and the fornicator", or: "the male thief and the female thief [are] among what Allah has prescribed for you"; and the meaning of this statement of theirs is: "among what has been prescribed for you is the ruling on the male thief and the female thief". Sībawayh said: the preferred choice in this in Arabic is the accusative, as you say ”زَيْدًا اضْرِبْهُ“ ("Zayd — strike him"); and he said: the generality refused to read it except with the nominative — by "the generality" he means the main body [of readers]. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read: ”والسّارِقَ والسّارِقَةَ فاقْطَعُوا أيْدِيَهُما“, and likewise ”اَلزّانِيَةَ والزّانِيَ“. This reading — even though its reader is eminent — I do not like it to be recited, because the main body is more worthy of being followed, since reading is a sunna (received practice). Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: my proof that the good reading is with the nominative in ”والزّانِيَةُ والزّانِي“ and in ”والسّارِقُ والسّارِقَةُ“ is His saying — exalted be His praise —: ﴿واللَّذانِ يَأْتِيانِها مِنكم فَآذُوهُما﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 16]. Someone other than Sībawayh among the Basrans — namely Muḥammad ibn Yazīd al-Mubarrad — said: I prefer ”والسّارِقُ والسّارِقَةُ“ to be nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), because the intent is not toward one specific person; so it is not like your saying ”زَيْدًا فاضْرِبْهُ“; it is only like your saying: "whoever steals, cut off his hand; and whoever fornicates, flog him". This view is the preferred one, and it is the position of some of the Basrans and the Kufans.
It is said that by ”أيْدِيَهُما“ is meant their right hands; and in the reading of Ibn Masʿūd: ”والسّارِقُونَ والسّارِقاتُ فاقْطَعُوا أيْمانَهم“. Some grammarians said: the dual of what a person has only one of was made [plural] only because most of his members are pairs, so what is single was treated like that. He said: because a person has two eyes, so when you put [the owners] in the dual you say ”عُيُونُهُما“ ("their [two persons'] eyes"); so ”قُلُوبُكُما“ and ”ظُهُورُهُما“ were made [plural] in the Qurʾān «[Translator's note: the source has فَجُعِلْتَ, apparently for فَجُعِلَتْ]», and likewise ”أيْدِيَهُما“. This is a mistake; rather, a distinction ought to be made between that of which a thing has one and that of which a thing has two. Some people said: we did that only to distinguish between that of which a thing has one and that of which a thing has two; so for that of which a thing has one, its dual was made a plural, as in the saying of Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿إنْ تَتُوبا إلى اللَّهِ فَقَدْ صَغَتْ قُلُوبُكُما﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 4]. Abū Isḥāq said: the truth of this section is that whatever a thing has only one of is not put in the dual but is pronounced in the form of the plural, because the annexation makes it clear: if you say ”أشْبَعْتُ بُطُونَهُما“ ("I filled their bellies"), it is known that the two have only two bellies. The origin of the dual is the plural, because when you make the singular dual you have gathered one to one; the original would have been to say ”اِثْنا رِجالٍ“ ("two of men"), but ”رَجُلانِ“ indicates the kind of thing and its number; so the dual is needed for brevity. When there is no [need for] brevity, the thing is returned to its origin, and its origin is the plural. So when you say ”قُلُوبُهُما“, the dual in ”هُما“ has made it unnecessary for you to put ”قَلْبٌ“ in the dual, and brevity here became leaving ”قَلْبٌ“ undualised. If what a thing has only one of is put in the dual, that is permissible according to the grammarians. The poet said:
ظَهْراهُما مِثْلُ ظُهُورِ التُّرْسَيْنِ
(Their two backs are like the backs of two shields.)
So he brought the dual and the plural in one verse. Sībawayh reported that the singular, and what is not part of something, may be put in the plural when you mean the dual; and it is reported from the Arabs: ”وَضَعا رِحالَهُما“ ("the two set down their saddles"), meaning the two saddles of their two mounts.
The jurists are unanimous that the thief's hand is cut off, whether free or slave, and that the female thief's hand is cut off, whether free or a slave-woman; and they are unanimous that the cutting is from the rusgh. ”اَلرُّسْغُ“ is the joint between the palm and the forearm (the wrist). One says ”رُسْغٌ“ and ”رُصْغٌ“, and [the form with] sīn is better.
﴿جَزاءً بِما كَسَبا﴾: ”جَزاءً“ is accusative because it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) «[Translator's note: so in the source; the paraphrase that follows ("as recompense for") fits a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), and مفعول به may be a slip for مفعول له.]»; the meaning: cut [their hands] as recompense for their deed. Likewise ﴿نَكالا مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾. And if you wish, both are accusative as the maṣdar (verbal noun) indicated by ”فاقْطَعُوا“, because the meaning of ”فاقْطَعُوا“ is: recompense them and make an exemplary punishment of them.

zajjaj:41-41.t:
His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿يا أيُّها الرَّسُولُ لا يَحْزُنْكَ الَّذِينَ يُسارِعُونَ في الكُفْرِ﴾: if you wish you say ”يَحْزُنْكَ“ and ”يَحْزَنْكَ“, with fatḥa and ḍamma, i.e. "let not their hastening into unbelief grieve you, since you have been promised victory over them" — and Allah knows best.
His saying: ﴿مِنَ الَّذِينَ قالُوا آمَنّا بِأفْواهِهِمْ ولَمْ تُؤْمِن قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾, i.e. let not the hastening into unbelief by the hypocrites and by those who are Jews grieve you. Then He said: ﴿سَمّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ سَمّاعُونَ لِقَوْمٍ آخَرِينَ لَمْ يَأْتُوكَ﴾ — this is the completion of the utterance. The nominative of ”سَمّاعُونَ“ is from two angles. One of them: "they are listeners to falsehood (هم سَمّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ)", i.e. the hypocrites and the Jews are listeners to falsehood. In ”سَمّاعُونَ“ there are two senses — and Allah knows best. One of them is that they are listeners to falsehood, i.e. accepters of falsehood, because a person hears truth and falsehood; but one says "do not listen to so-and-so's word", i.e. do not accept his word; and of this is ”سَمِعَ اللَّهُ لِمَن حَمِدَهُ“, i.e. Allah has accepted his praise. So its interpretation is that they accept falsehood. The other sense of ”سَمّاعُونَ“ is that its meaning is that they listen to you in order to lie about you; that is, when they sat with him it became possible for them to say: "we heard such-and-such from him".
﴿سَمّاعُونَ لِقَوْمٍ آخَرِينَ﴾, i.e. they listen to you on behalf of other people ﴿لَمْ يَأْتُوكَ﴾, i.e. they are spies for those absent ones. And it is possible that the nominative of ”سَمّاعُونَ“ is on the meaning "and among those who are Jews are listeners (وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ هادُوا سَمّاعُونَ)", so that the information is that the listeners are among them, and it is raised by ”مِنهم“, as you say ”في قَوْمِكَ عُقَلاءُ“ ("among your people are wise men"). This is the position of al-Akhfash; and Sībawayh held that this is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
His saying: ﴿يُحَرِّفُونَ الكَلِمَ مِن بَعْدِ مَواضِعِهِ﴾, i.e. after Allah has put it in its place, i.e. prescribed its obligations, made its lawful lawful and its unlawful unlawful.
His saying: ﴿إنْ أُوتِيتُمْ هَذا فَخُذُوهُ وإنْ لَمْ تُؤْتَوْهُ فاحْذَرُوا﴾: if you are given this distorted ruling, take it; and if you are not given it, beware, i.e. beware if the Prophet ﷺ gives you a fatwa other than what we have laid down for you — beware of acting on it. The cause of this, according to what is related, is «that fornication became widespread among the nobles of the Jews and Khaybar. In the Torah it was [laid down] that the two muḥṣan (married) persons are to be stoned. A man and a woman fornicated, and the Jews hoped that flogging had been revealed to the Prophet ﷺ for the two muḥṣan persons; they had distorted [the Torah] and had taken to flogging the two muḥṣan persons and blackening their faces. So Allah — exalted be His praise — revealed [to him] that they would seek his fatwa about the matter of these two women «[Translator's note: so in the source (هاتَيْنِ المَرْأتَيْنِ); the account concerns a man and a woman.]», and informed him that Allah commanded them [to be asked] about the most learned of them in the Torah «[Translator's note: the wording يَأْمُرُهم عَنْ أعْلَمِهِمْ is so in the source and appears disturbed.]». They told him that he was not present; the Prophet ﷺ said: "I know [where he is]" — Jibrīl had informed him of his whereabouts — and he ordered them to bring him, and they brought him. Allah revealed to His Prophet that he should make them swear that they would tell him the truth. When their scholar came, the Prophet said to him: "I ask you by the One who sent down the Torah to Mūsā, raised the Mount above you and parted the sea for you: is it in the Torah that the two muḥṣan persons are to be stoned if they fornicate?" He said: "Yes." The rabble of the Jews leapt upon him, and he said: "I feared that if I belied him a punishment would come down upon us."» It is said that the one whom the Prophet ﷺ asked was Ibn Ṣūriyā the Jew, who was young in age; the Prophet ﷺ said to him: "Are you the most learned of your people in the Torah?" He said: "So they say." He was the one who informed him that stoning was in it; and he asked the Prophet ﷺ about things which he knew [to be] among his signs, and when the Prophet ﷺ told him about them he said: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that you are the Messenger of Allah, the unlettered Arab Prophet whom the messengers foretold." What we have mentioned about the matter of the two adulterers is well known in the transmission of the exegetes, and it makes clear His saying: ﴿إنْ أُوتِيتُمْ هَذا فَخُذُوهُ وإنْ لَمْ تُؤْتَوْهُ فاحْذَرُوا﴾; someone might say: what is the explanation of this? Therefore we have explained it; and with Allah is all power and strength.
His saying: ﴿وَمَن يُرِدِ اللَّهُ فِتْنَتَهُ﴾: it is said: his exposure; and it is also said: his unbelief; and it may be: testing him with what makes his affair manifest. One says ”فَتَنْتُ الحَدِيدَ“ when I have heated the iron, and ”فَتَنْتُ الرَّجُلَ“ when I have moved the man away from what he was upon; and of this is His saying: ﴿وَإنْ كادُوا لَيَفْتِنُونَكَ عَنِ الَّذِي أوْحَيْنا إلَيْكَ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 73], i.e. and they almost moved you away.
His saying: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ لَمْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ أنْ يُطَهِّرَ قُلُوبَهُمْ﴾, i.e. to humiliate them «[Translator's note: so in the source (أيْ: أنْ يُهِينَهُمُ); as written it does not gloss "purify their hearts" naturally, and the text may be disturbed.]». ﴿لَهم في الدُّنْيا خِزْيٌ﴾: it is said: they have in this world exposure through what Allah has made manifest of their lying; and it is said: they have disgrace in this world through the taking of the jizya from them and the imposing of humiliation and wretchedness upon them.

zajjaj:42-42.t:
Then He — Mighty and Majestic is He — returned to describing them, saying: ﴿سَمّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ أكّالُونَ لِلسُّحْتِ﴾; it is also read ”لِلسُّحُتِ“ — both. Its interpretation is that the bribes which they consume — Allah will punish them for them by annihilating them (yusḥituhum) with punishment, as He — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿لا تَفْتَرُوا عَلى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا فَيُسْحِتَكم بِعَذابٍ﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 61]. Like this is His saying: ﴿إنَّما يَأْكُلُونَ في بُطُونِهِمْ نارًا﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 10], i.e. they consume that whose outcome is the Fire. One says ”سَحَتَهُ، وأسْحَتَهُ“ when he has extirpated it. Some said: ”سَحَتَهُ“ means he took it away little by little until he extirpated it. Like ”أسْحَتَهُ“ is the saying of al-Farazdaq:
وَعَضُّ زَمانٍ يا ابْنَ مَرْوانَ لَمْ يَدَعْ ∗∗∗ مِنَ المالِ إلّا مُسْحَتًا أوْ مُجَلَّفُ
(And the bite of a time, O son of Marwān, which left of wealth nothing but what was wiped out or stripped down to a remnant.)
It is possible that ”سَحَتَهُ“ and ”أسْحَتَهُ“ [both] mean when he extirpated it, whether that was little by little or all at once.
His saying: ﴿فَإنْ جاءُوكَ فاحْكم بَيْنَهم أوْ أعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ﴾: the scholars are unanimous that this verse indicates that the Prophet ﷺ was given the choice by it in judging between the protected people (ahl al-dhimma). It is said in some of the views that the choice was abrogated by His saying: ﴿وَأنِ احْكم بَيْنَهم بِما أنْـزَلَ اللَّهُ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 49].
His saying: ﴿فاحْكم بَيْنَهم بِالقِسْطِ﴾, i.e. with justice.

zajjaj:44-44.t:
His saying: ﴿إنّا أنْـزَلْنا التَّوْراةَ فِيها هُدًى ونُورٌ يَحْكُمُ بِها النَّبِيُّونَ﴾, i.e. in it is light, i.e. a clarification that the matter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is true, and in it is the clarification of the ruling about which they came seeking the fatwa of the Prophet ﷺ. It is possible that the meaning is by way of fronting and postponement (al-taqdīm wa-l-taʾkhīr), in the sense: "We sent down the Torah, in which is guidance and light for those who are Jews (لِلَّذِينَ هادُوا); by it the prophets who submitted, and the rabbis, judge". And it is possible that [it is] ﴿يَحْكُمُ بِها النَّبِيُّونَ الَّذِينَ أسْلَمُوا لِلَّذِينَ هادُوا﴾, i.e. the Prophet ﷺ judges in what they asked him by what is in the Torah. And it is possible that ﴿لِلَّذِينَ هادُوا﴾ means "for those who repented", i.e. the prophets and the rabbānīs — who are the scholars and the aḥbār, the excellent scholars — judge for those who repent from unbelief. ﴿بِما اسْتُحْفِظُوا مِن كِتابِ اللَّهِ﴾, i.e. [what] was entrusted to them.
His saying: ﴿وَمَن لَمْ يَحْكم بِما أنْـزَلَ اللَّهُ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الكافِرُونَ﴾, i.e. whoever claims that one of the rulings of Allah which the prophets — peace be upon them — brought is false, is an unbeliever. The jurists are unanimous that whoever says that the two muḥṣan persons need not be stoned if they fornicate, being free, is an unbeliever. Whoever rejects one of the rulings of the Prophet ﷺ is declared an unbeliever only because he is belying him, and whoever belies the Prophet is an unbeliever.

zajjaj:45-45.t:
His saying: ﴿وَكَتَبْنا عَلَيْهِمْ فِيها﴾, i.e. in the Torah, ﴿أنَّ النَّفْسَ بِالنَّفْسِ والعَيْنَ بِالعَيْنِ﴾. It is related that the Prophet recited: ”والعَيْنُ بِالعَيْنِ“. The reading is ﴿والعَيْنَ بِالعَيْنِ والأنْفَ بِالأنْفِ والأُذُنَ بِالأُذُنِ والسِّنَّ بِالسِّنِّ والجُرُوحَ قِصاصٌ﴾ with both the nominative and the accusative; there is no disagreement among the people of Arabic about that. Whoever reads ”اَلْعَيْنَ بِالعَيْنِ“ intends ”أنَّ العَيْنَ بِالعَيْنِ“ ("that the eye is for the eye"). Whoever reads ”والعَيْنُ بِالعَيْنِ“, its nominative is on two grounds: [first,] by conjunction to the position of ”اَلنَّفْسَ بِالنَّفْسِ“ and what governs it; the meaning is: "and We prescribed for them: the soul for the soul", i.e. "We said to them: the soul for the soul". The kasra of ”إنَّ“ (i.e. إنَّ النَّفْسَ) is permissible, but I know of no one who read it so; so do not read it unless a sound transmission is established. And it is possible that ”اَلْعَيْنُ بِالعَيْنِ“ is nominative as a fresh start (ʿalā al-istiʾnāf, resumptive). And there is another aspect in it: it may be conjoined to the pronoun implied in ”اَلنَّفْسَ“ «[Translator's note: i.e. the pronoun latent in the predicate بِالنَّفْسِ]», because the pronoun implied in ”اَلنَّفْسَ“ is in the nominative position; the meaning is: "that the soul is taken — it — for the soul", and ”اَلْعَيْنُ“ is conjoined to ”هي“ ("it").
His saying: ﴿فَمَن تَصَدَّقَ بِهِ فَهو كَفّارَةٌ لَهُ﴾: some said: whoever gives it up as charity, i.e. his right, it is an expiation for the one who wounded: if the wounded person forgoes his right, retaliation is lifted from the one who wounded. Others said: it is an expiation for the wounded person, i.e. Allah expiates from him, by his pardon, his past sins.

zajjaj:48-48.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمُهَيْمِنًا عَلَيْهِ﴾: some transmitted it as ”وَمُهَيْمَنًا“, with fatḥa on the second mīm; it is [good] Arabic, but I do not like reading it so, because there is consensus in the reading on the kasra of the mīm in His saying: ﴿المُؤْمِنُ المُهَيْمِنُ﴾ [al-Ḥashr: 23]. People differed in explaining His saying: ﴿المُؤْمِنُ المُهَيْمِنُ﴾ [al-Ḥashr: 23], and people differed in explaining His saying: ﴿وَمُهَيْمِنًا عَلَيْهِ﴾. «[Translator's note: the clause about al-Ḥashr: 23 appears thus, apparently duplicated, in the source.]» Some said: its meaning is "and a witness over it"; some said: "a watcher over it"; some said: its meaning is "entrusted with it"; and some said: ”اَلْمُهَيْمِنُ“ is one of the names of Allah in the ancient scriptures. Some said: ”مُهَيْمِنٌ“ has the meaning of ”مُؤْتَمَنٌ“ ("entrusted"), except that the hāʾ is a substitute for the hamza, the origin being ”مُؤْتَمَنًا عَلَيْهِ“, just as they said ”هَرَقْتُ الماءَ“ and ”أرَقْتُ الماءَ“ ("I poured out the water"), and as they said ”إيّاكَ“ and ”هِيّاكَ“. This is the view of Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad], and according to the method of Arabic it is good and agrees with some of what has come in the exegesis, because its meaning is ”مُؤْتَمَنٌ“.
His saying: ﴿وَلْيَحْكم أهْلُ الإنْجِيلِ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 47]: it was read with the lām unvowelled and the mīm in the jussive, on the pattern of the command; and it was read ”وَلِيَحْكُمَ“, with kasra on the lām and fatḥa on the mīm, in the sense of ”وَلِأنْ يَحْكُمَ“ ("and so that [the people of the Gospel] may judge"). The kasra of the lām with the jussive is permissible: ”وَلِيَحْكم أهْلُ الإنْجِيلِ“, but it has not been read so as far as I know. The origin was the kasra of the lām, but the kasra was dropped for lightness. As for ”اَلْإنْجِيلِ“, the reading in it is with kasra on the hamza; and it is related from al-Ḥasan: ”اَلْأنْجِيلِ“, with fatḥa on the hamza. This is a weak view, because ”أنْجِيلٌ“ would be [the pattern] ”أفْعِيلٌ“, and this pattern does not exist in the speech of the Arabs, whereas ”إنْجِيلٌ“ is ”إفْعِيلٌ“ from ”اَلنَّجْلُ“, which is the origin (root/source). But one might say: ”إنْجِيلٌ“ is a foreign noun, so it is not objectionable that it occur with fatḥa on the hamza, because many foreign nouns differ from the patterns of the Arabs, such as ”آجُرُّ“ (baked brick), ”إبْراهِيمُ“, ”هابِيلُ“ and ”قابِيلُ“; so it is not objectionable that ”أنْجِيلٌ“ should occur. I disliked reading it so only because, as for its chain of transmission from al-Ḥasan, I do not know whether it comes from a trustworthy quarter or not.

zajjaj:101-101.t:
His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَسْألُوا عَنْ أشْياءَ إنْ تُبْدَ لَكم تَسُؤْكم وإنْ تَسْألُوا عَنْها حِينَ يُنَـزَّلُ القُرْآنُ تُبْدَ لَكُمْ﴾: "تُبْدَ لَكم" means: (if) they are made manifest to you. One says "بَدا لِيَ الشَّيْءُ، يَبْدُو" when it has become manifest. It has come in the tafsīr «that the Prophet ﷺ addressed the people and informed them that Allah had made the Ḥajj obligatory upon them. A man from Banū Asad stood and said: "O Messenger of Allah, is it every year?" He ﷺ turned away from him. The man repeated it a second time, and he turned away from him; then he repeated it a third time, and he ﷺ said: "What makes you feel safe that I might say 'Yes', so that it becomes obligatory, and then you do not carry it out, and so you disbelieve?"» The interpretation of "you disbelieve" here — and Allah knows best — is that you would reject its obligation because of its burden, and so disbelieve. And he ﷺ said: «Leave me as long as I leave you, for those before you were destroyed only by their much questioning and disagreeing with their prophets.» And a man about whom two men were disputing, each of them claiming that he was his father, asked him ﷺ, and he ﷺ told him which of them was his father. So Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known that asking about things of this kind ought not to take place, for when the answer to it is made manifest, that brings distress — especially at the time of asking the Prophet ﷺ by way of the clarification of the verses. So Allah forbade that, and made known that He has pardoned them; and there is no justification for asking about what Allah has forbidden, and it involves a disgrace for the asker if it is made manifest.
"أشْياءَ" is in the position of the genitive, except that it was given fatḥa because it is a diptote. Al-Kisāʾī said: its ending resembled the ending of "حَمْراءُ", and its pattern according to him is "أفْعالُ"; their use of it became frequent, so it was made diptote. The Basrans and most of the Kufans agreed that al-Kisāʾī's view in this is a mistake, and they bound him (by consequence) to not inflecting "أبْناءٌ" and "أسْماءٌ" as triptotes. Al-Akhfash — Saʿīd ibn Masʿada — and al-Farrāʾ said: its original form is "أفْعِلاءُ", as you say "هَيْنٌ" and "أهْوِناءُ", except that the original was "أشْيِئاءُ", on the pattern "أشْبِعاعٌ" [Translator's note: so in the text]; two hamzas came together with an alif between them, so the first hamza was dropped. This is also a mistake, because "شَيْءٌ" [Translator's note: the text has «شَيْئًا»] is "فَعْلٌ", and "فَعْلٌ" is not pluralised as "أفْعِلاءُ". As for "هَيْنٌ", its original form is "أهْيِنٌ" [Translator's note: so in the text; presumably «هَيِّنٌ» is intended], so it was pluralised as "أفْعِلاءُ", just as "فَعِيلٌ" is pluralised as "أفْعِلاءُ", like "نَصِيبٌ" and "أنْصِباءُ". Al-Khalīl said: "أشْياءُ" is a collective noun (ism li-l-jamīʿ); its original was "فَعْلاءُ", "شَيْئاءُ"; the two hamzas were found heavy, so the first was moved to the beginning of the word, and it was made "لَفْعاءُ", just as they said "أنْوُقٌ" and transposed it to "أيْنُقٌ", and as they transposed "قُوُوسٌ" and said "قِسِيٌّ". Their pluralising "أشْياءُ" as "أشاوِي" and "أشاياهٌ" confirms al-Khalīl's view. Al-Khalīl's view is the doctrine of Sībawayh, Abū ʿUthmān al-Māzinī and all the Basrans, except al-Ziyādī among them, who inclined to the view of al-Akhfash. They mentioned that al-Māzinī debated al-Akhfash on this and silenced him: he asked him, "How do you form the diminutive of 'أشْياءُ'?" He said: "'أُشَيّاءُ'." So know (this): had it been "أفْعِلاءُ", it would have been returned in the diminutive to its singular, and it would have been said "شُيَيْئاتٌ"; and the consensus of the Basrans is that the diminutive of "أصْدِقاءُ" (friends), if it is for feminines, is "صُدَيِّقاتٌ", and if it is for masculines, "صُدَيِّقُونَ".

zajjaj:103-103.t: His saying: ﴿ما جَعَلَ اللَّهُ مِن بَحِيرَةٍ ولا سائِبَةٍ ولا وصِيلَةٍ ولا حامٍ﴾: the most reliable of what we have transmitted from the lexicographers on the explanation of these names is what I mention here. The lexicographers said: "اَلْبَحِيرَةُ" was a she-camel which, when she had borne five litters and the last of them was a male, they would slit (نَحَرُوا) her ear — that is, they split it — and they refrained from riding her and slaughtering her; she would not be driven away from water nor kept from pasture, and if an exhausted man met her he would not ride her. "اَلسّائِبَةُ": when a man made a vow for (his) return from a journey, or recovery from an illness, or the like, he would say: "This she-camel of mine is sāʾiba (let loose)", and she was like the baḥīra in that no benefit was taken from her, she was not driven away from water, and she was not kept from pasture. And when a man freed a slave, he would say: "He is sāʾiba", and then there was no blood-money liability (ʿaql) between them, nor inheritance. As for "اَلْوَصِيلَةُ", it is among sheep: when a ewe bore a female, it was theirs, and when she bore a male and a female, they said: "She has joined (وَصَلَتْ) her brother", so they did not slaughter the male for their gods. As for "اَلْحامِي", it is the male among camels: when ten litters had been born from the stallion's loins, the Arabs would protect (حُمِيَ) his back, so no load was put on him, and he was not kept from water or pasture. So Allah made known that He had not forbidden anything of these things, and that those who disbelieve fabricated (it) against Allah.

zajjaj:105-105.t:
His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا عَلَيْكم أنْفُسَكُمْ﴾: its meaning is: Allah has only made you responsible for the affair of your own selves.
﴿لا يَضُرُّكم مَن ضَلَّ إذا اهْتَدَيْتُمْ﴾, that is: Allah will not hold you accountable for the sins of others. The wording of this verse does not require abandoning commanding the right and forbidding the wrong; He made known that the disbelief of the disbeliever does not harm the believer. But if the believer abandons commanding the right while he is able to do so, he is astray and not rightly guided. The i'rab of "لا يَضُرُّكم مَن ضَلَّ": the best is that it be nominative (indicative), as a statement (khabar), the meaning being: "the one who strays does not harm you if you are rightly guided". It may be that its position is jussive (jazm), the original being "لا يَضْرُرْكم", except that the first rāʾ was assimilated into the second, and the second was given ḍamma because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. In Arabic, by way of prohibition, "لا يَضُرَّكم" with fatḥa on the rāʾ and "لا يَضُرِّكم" with kasra are permissible, but the (established) recitation is not to be contradicted, and also because the ḍamma is better, whether the position is nominative or jussive. As for whoever gives ḍamma for the meeting of two quiescents, he makes the ḍamma follow the ḍamma; as for whoever gives kasra, it is because kasra is the basic (vowel) for the meeting of two quiescents; and as for whoever gives fatḥa, he gives fatḥa for the meeting of two quiescents because of the lightness of fatḥa. This prohibition is in the wording of the absent (third person) while those addressed are meant: when you say "لا يَضْرُرْكَ كُفْرُ الكافِرِ" (let not the disbeliever's disbelief harm you), the meaning is: "do not count his disbelief as harm"; just as when you say "لا أرَيَنَّكَ هَهُنا" (let me not see you here), the prohibition in the wording is to yourself, but its meaning is to the one you address; its meaning is: "do not be here".

zajjaj:106-106.t:
His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا شَهادَةُ بَيْنِكم إذا حَضَرَ أحَدَكُمُ المَوْتُ حِينَ الوَصِيَّةِ اثْنانِ ذَوا عَدْلٍ مِنكُمْ﴾: its meaning is that the testimony at the time of the bequest is for (the case of) death — not that death is present to him while he makes his bequest — by what the testator says, whether he is healthy or not healthy: "When death comes to me — or when I die — then do (such)... and carry out (such)...". "Testimony" is nominative from two aspects. One of them is that it is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is "اِثْنانِ", the meaning being: "The testimony of this situation is the testimony of two"; then "شَهادَةُ" is omitted and "اِثْنانِ" stands in its place.
And the nominative of "شَهادَةُ بَيْنِكم" may be according to (the sense of) His saying: "and among what Allah has prescribed for you regarding your testimony is that two should testify", so "اِثْنانِ" is made nominative by "شَهادَةُ", the meaning being: "that two upright men from among you should testify". Regarding the meaning of "مِنكم", two views were stated. Some said: "مِنكم" means: from the people of your religion, ﴿أوْ آخَرانِ مِن غَيْرِكُمْ﴾: from other than the people of your religion. Others said: "ذَوا عَدْلٍ مِنكم" means: from the family of the deceased, "أوْ آخَرانِ مِن غَيْرِكم": from other than the family of the deceased. These argued that His saying ﴿فَيُقْسِمانِ بِاللَّهِ إنِ ارْتَبْتُمْ لا نَشْتَرِي بِهِ ثَمَنًا ولَوْ كانَ ذا قُرْبى﴾ indicates that "مِنكم" means: from those of your kinship. These said: also, when they are upright and of the kin of the deceased, they are more fitting, because they know the circumstances of the family better than strangers do, and know better what is good for them. They also argued that ﴿ذَوا عَدْلٍ﴾ (two upright men) cannot be from other than the people of the religion of Islam, because disbelief has put (one) far from uprightness. So Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known that the two witnesses of a bequest ought to be two upright men from the family of the deceased or from other than his family, if the testator is resident; and likewise if he is on a journey. For His saying ﴿إنْ أنْتُمْ ضَرَبْتُمْ في الأرْضِ فَأصابَتْكم مُصِيبَةُ المَوْتِ﴾ mentions death on a journey after His saying ﴿إذا حَضَرَ أحَدَكُمُ المَوْتُ حِينَ الوَصِيَّةِ﴾; so it is as though there is in the verse — and Allah knows best — an indication regarding testimony both when resident and on a journey. It has come in the tafsīr that two non-Muslims had testified on a journey; and (against this) there is the consensus that witnesses are not required to swear. Some have permitted the testimony of two dhimmīs on a journey. Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿وَأشْهِدُوا ذَوَيْ عَدْلٍ مِنكم وأقِيمُوا الشَّهادَةَ لِلَّهِ﴾ [al-Ṭalāq: 2], and said: ﴿مِمَّنْ تَرْضَوْنَ مِنَ الشُّهَداءِ﴾ [al-Baqara: 282]. When a witness is known to be a liar, it is not permissible to accept his testimony; and we know that the Christians claimed that Allah is the third of three, and that the Jews said that ʿUzayr is the son of Allah, and we know that they are liars; so how can the testimony of one who persists in lying be accepted? As for the meaning of His saying ﴿تَحْبِسُونَهُما مِن بَعْدِ الصَّلاةِ فَيُقْسِمانِ بِاللَّهِ﴾: people in the Ḥijāz used to swear (oaths) after the ʿAṣr prayer, because it is the time when people gather.
His saying: ﴿إنِ ارْتَبْتُمْ﴾: if doubt about them occurs in your souls, that is: you suspect them of something doubtful.

zajjaj:107-107.t:
His saying: ﴿فَإنْ عُثِرَ عَلى أنَّهُما اسْتَحَقّا إثْمًا﴾, that is: if it is discovered that they have both acted treacherously, ﴿فَآخَرانِ يَقُومانِ مَقامَهُما مِنَ الَّذِينَ اسْتَحَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ الأوْلَيانِ﴾. It has been read "اَلْأوَّلِينَ", and "مِنَ الَّذِينَ اسْتَحَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ الأوْلَيانِ" is permissible [Translator's note: so in the text; a different vocalisation, e.g. the passive «اسْتُحِقَّ», is presumably meant]. This is one of the most difficult places in the Quran as regards i'rab. "أوْلَيانِ", according to the view of most of the Basrans, are nominative as a badal (substitute) of what is in "يَقُومانِ" (its pronoun); the meaning is: "Let the two nearest to the deceased stand in the place of these two treacherous ones", and they swear by Allah: our testimony is truer than their testimony.
When "اَلْأوْلَيانِ" is nominative as a badal, then what is in "اِسْتَحَقَّ" of the pronoun has the sense of the bequest; the meaning is: "Let the two nearest stand, from those against whom the bequest has become due, or against whom the bequeathing has become due". Some said: the meaning of "مِنَ الَّذِينَ اسْتَحَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ الأوْلَيانِ" is: "it has become due among them (فِيهِمْ)", "عَلى" standing in place of "في", just as "في" stood in place of "عَلى" in His saying: ﴿وَلأُصَلِّبَنَّكم في جُذُوعِ النَّخْلِ﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 71], meaning: on the trunks of the palm trees. And some said: the meaning of "عَلى" in "مِنَ الَّذِينَ اسْتَحَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ الأوْلَيانِ" is (that of "مِن"), as He said: ﴿الَّذِينَ إذا اكْتالُوا عَلى النّاسِ يَسْتَوْفُونَ﴾ [al-Muṭaffifīn: 2], that is: when they take measure from people. And it was said: in "اِسْتَحَقَّ" there is reference to the sin, because in His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿فَإنْ عُثِرَ عَلى أنَّهُما اسْتَحَقّا إثْمًا فَآخَرانِ يَقُومانِ مَقامَهُما مِنَ الَّذِينَ اسْتَحَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ الأوْلَيانِ﴾ the meaning was: "those against whom the sin was committed". And it was said that "اَلْأوْلَيانِ" may be nominative by "اِسْتَحَقَّ", their meaning being: "the two most entitled to the oath", that is: to making those who testify after them swear. If the testimony of the two Christians is permissible, then "اَلْأوْلَيانِ" on this view are "the two Christians", or the other two from outside the household of the deceased. The best of these views is that "اَلْأوْلَيانِ" be a badal, with the meaning: "Let the two nearest stand, from those against whom the bequest has become due". Whoever read "اَلْأوَّلِينَ" referred it back to "اَلَّذِينَ", and the meaning was: "from those first ones against whom the bequeathing has become due". The one who read so argued, saying: what do you think if the two nearest were minors?

zajjaj:108-108.t: His saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ أدْنى أنْ يَأْتُوا بِالشَّهادَةِ عَلى وجْهِها﴾, that is: that is nearer to bringing the testimony in its proper form, and nearer to their fearing.

zajjaj:109-109.t: His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ يَجْمَعُ اللَّهُ الرُّسُلَ فَيَقُولُ ماذا أُجِبْتُمْ﴾: as for the accusative of "يَوْمَ", it is construed with His saying: ﴿واتَّقُوا اللَّهَ واسْمَعُوا﴾ [al-Māʾida: 108], that is: and fear the Day on which Allah will gather the messengers, as He said: ﴿واتَّقُوا يَوْمًا لا تَجْزِي نَفْسٌ عَنْ نَفْسٍ شَيْئًا﴾ [al-Baqara: 48]. The meaning of the questioning of the messengers by Allah the Exalted is by way of rebuke to those to whom they were sent, as He — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿وَإذا المَوْءُودَةُ سُئِلَتْ﴾ [al-Takwīr: 8] ﴿بِأيِّ ذَنْبٍ قُتِلَتْ﴾ [al-Takwīr: 9]: she is only asked so that her killers may be rebuked. As for the messengers' answer and their saying "لا عِلْمَ لَنا" (we have no knowledge), people have said more than one thing about this. It has come in some of the tafsīr that their understanding left them because of the terror of the Day of Resurrection, so they said: "We have no knowledge alongside Your knowledge". Some said: had their understanding left them, they would not have said: ﴿إنَّكَ أنْتَ عَلامُ الغُيُوبِ﴾. And some said: the meaning of the messengers' saying "لا عِلْمَ لَنا" is: (we have no knowledge) of what was hidden from us of those to whom we were sent; You, our Lord, know their inner selves, and we do not know what is hidden of them; ﴿إنَّكَ أنْتَ عَلّامُ الغُيُوبِ﴾.

zajjaj:110-110.t:
His saying: ﴿إذْ قالَ اللَّهُ يا عِيسى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ اذْكُرْ نِعْمَتِي عَلَيْكَ وعَلى والِدَتِكَ﴾: as for His favour upon his mother, it is that He chose her, purified her and chose her above the women of the worlds, and her provision used to come to her from Him while she was in her sanctuary (miḥrāb).
His saying: ﴿إذْ أيَّدْتُكَ بِرُوحِ القُدُسِ﴾, that is: I supported you with Jibrīl. It is possible that He strengthened him with him when the Children of Israel attempted to kill him, and it is possible that He supported him with him in all his circumstances, because there is an indication of that in the speech.
His saying: ﴿تُكَلِّمُ النّاسَ في المَهْدِ﴾, that is: I supported you, (you) speaking to people in the cradle; ﴿وَكَهْلا﴾, that is: I supported you as a man of mature age. And it is possible that "وَكَهْلًا" is construed with "تُكَلِّمُ", the meaning being: I supported you, addressing people in your infancy and addressing people as a man of mature age. Some read "أأْيَدْتُكَ" on the pattern "أفْعَلْتُكَ", from "اَلْأيْدُ" (strength), and some read "آيَدْتُكَ" on the pattern "فاعَلْتُكَ", that is: I aided you.
His saying: ﴿وَتُبْرِئُ الأكْمَهَ والأبْرَصَ بِإذْنِي﴾: "اَلْأكْمَهُ" — some said: the one who is born blind. Al-Khalīl said: it is the one who is born blind, and it is the one who becomes blind after having been sighted.

zajjaj:111-111.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَإذْ أوْحَيْتُ إلى الحَوارِيِّينَ أنْ آمِنُوا بِي وبِرَسُولِي﴾: some said: "أوْحَيْتُ إلى الحَوارِيِّينَ" means: I inspired them, as He said: ﴿وَأوْحى رَبُّكَ إلى النَّحْلِ أنِ اتَّخِذِي مِنَ الجِبالِ بُيُوتًا﴾ [al-Naḥl: 68], that is: He inspired it. Some said: "أوْحَيْتُ إلى الحَوارِيِّينَ" means: He commanded them; and they recited the poet's saying:
؎اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي استَهَلَّتْ ∗∗∗ بِإذْنِهِ السَّماءُ واطْمَأنَّتْ
أوْحى لَها القَرارَ فاسْتَقَرَّتْ
(Praise be to Allah, by whose leave the sky poured down rain and then became still; He commanded it to settle, and it settled.)
They said: its meaning is: He commanded it. And some said: the meaning of "وَإذْ أوْحَيْتُ إلى الحَوارِيِّينَ" is: I brought them, in the revelation to you, the proofs and signs by which they inferred (the way) to faith, so they believed in Me.

zajjaj:112-112.t:
His saying: ﴿إذْ قالَ الحَوارِيُّونَ يا عِيسى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ﴾: it is possible that the position of "عِيسى" is accusative, as you say "يا زَيْدَ بْنَ عَمْرٍو", because when "اِبْنٌ" is annexed to a known proper name, or annexed to a known kunya (agnomen), it and what precedes it are treated as a single thing. All the grammarians choose "يا زَيْدَ بْنَ عَمْرٍو", and all of them permit "يا زَيْدُ بْنَ عَمْرٍو"; accordingly, the position of "عِيسى" may be the position of a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma. They all said: if you say "يا زَيْدُ ابْنَ أخِينا" (O Zayd, son of our brother) and "يا زَيْدُ ابْنَ الرَّجُلِ الصّالِحِ" (O Zayd, son of the righteous man), you give "زَيْدًا" ḍamma and nothing else, because the accusative only occurs when "اِبْنٌ" is annexed to a proper name, as we described. It has been read "هَلْ تَسْتَطِيعُ رَبَّكَ" and ﴿هَلْ يَسْتَطِيعُ رَبُّكَ﴾. Whoever read "هَلْ تَسْتَطِيعُ رَبَّكَ", the meaning is: "Can you call for His response and His compliance in sending down to us...?" And whoever read it "هَلْ يَسْتَطِيعُ رَبُّكَ", its meaning was: "Is your Lord able?" Abū Isḥāq [Translator's note: al-Zajjāj himself] said: the meaning in my view — and Allah knows best — is not that they were ignorant that Allah is able to send down a table, but the thrust of the question is: "Will you show us that your Lord will show us what we have asked, for your sake, of your signs which indicate your prophethood?" As for "اَلْمائِدَةُ", Abū ʿUbayda said: in meaning it is "مَفْعُولَةٌ" (passive participle) while its wording is "فاعِلَةٌ" (active participle); he said: it is like ﴿عِيشَةٍ راضِيَةٍ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 21]. And he said: al-māʾida is from giving, and "اَلْمُمْتادُ" is the iftaʿala form, the one from whom giving is sought. The poet said:
؎إنِّي أمِيرُ المُؤْمِنِينَ المُمْتادْ
(I am the Commander of the Faithful, the one from whom bounty is sought.)
And "مادَ زَيْدٌ عَمْرًا" (Zayd gave to ʿAmr) when he gave to him. The origin of "مائِدَةٌ" in my view is that it is "فاعِلَةٌ" from "مادَ، يَمِيدُ" when it moves, as though it sways with what is on it. It was said in the tafsīr that it was sent down upon them on Sunday, and on it were bread and fish; so the Christians make Sunday a feast — according to what was said — because of that. Some said that it was not sent down, because of the tahawwud [Translator's note: so in the text («لِلتَّهَوُّدِ»); perhaps «التَّهْدِيدِ», "the threat", is meant] that occurred regarding disbelief after its sending down. The more likely is that it was (sent down), because its sending down is mentioned in this story; Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿إنِّي مُنَـزِّلُها عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 115]. And non-Muslims said that it was sent down, and the reports (about it) have reached (us), so believing in it is obligatory. As for the reason for the disciples' asking ʿĪsā for the table, it bears two aspects: one of them is that they sought to increase in firmness, as Ibrāhīm said: ﴿رَبِّ أرِنِي كَيْفَ تُحْيِ المَوْتى﴾ [al-Baqara: 260]; and it is possible that their asking for the table was before their knowing that he had healed the one born blind and the leper and that he had brought the dead to life. As for ʿĪsā's saying to the disciples: اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ (fear Allah if you are believers), he only commanded them not to propose signs themselves, and not to put themselves forward before Allah and His Messenger, because Allah had shown them the signs and proofs through the bringing of the dead to life, and that is more conclusive than what they asked for and sought.

zajjaj:114-114.t: His saying: ﴿قالَ عِيسى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّنا﴾: Sībawayh mentioned that "اَللَّهُمَّ" is like an interjection (ṣawt), and that it does not take a qualifier, and that "رَبَّنا" is accusative by another vocative. We have explained this before in full. The meaning of His saying ﴿وَآيَةً مِنكَ﴾ is: so that it may be for us a sign from You.

zajjaj:115-115.t: As for His saying: ﴿فَإنِّي أُعَذِّبُهُ عَذابًا لا أُعَذِّبُهُ أحَدًا مِنَ العالَمِينَ﴾, it is possible that He hastens the punishment for them in this world, and it is possible that it is in the Hereafter, because of His saying: ﴿لا أُعَذِّبُهُ أحَدًا مِنَ العالَمِينَ﴾.

zajjaj:116-116.t: His saying: ﴿أأنْتَ قُلْتَ لِلنّاسِ اتَّخِذُونِي وأُمِّيَ إلَهَيْنِ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾: the questioning here is by way of rebuke to those who made claims against him, because they are agreed that he is truthful in what he reports and that he does not lie to them, and he is the truthful one in their view; so that is more conclusive as an argument against them and more effective in rebuking them, and rebuke is a kind of punishment. ﴿قالَ سُبْحانَكَ﴾, that is: You are free of evil. ﴿ما يَكُونُ لِي أنْ أقُولَ ما لَيْسَ لِي بِحَقٍّ﴾. As for His saying: ﴿تَعْلَمُ ما في نَفْسِي ولا أعْلَمُ ما في نَفْسِكَ إنَّكَ أنْتَ عَلامُ الغُيُوبِ﴾: "اَلْغِيُوبِ" (is said) with kasra and with ḍamma. Abū Isḥāq said: this is a place — I mean "تَعْلَمُ ما في نَفْسِي ولا أعْلَمُ ما في نَفْسِكَ" — with which the heretics confuse those whose knowledge of the language is weak, and the reality of it is known only from the language. The lexicographers said: "اَلنَّفْسُ" in the speech of the Arabs is used in two ways. One of them is your saying: "خَرَجَتْ نَفْسُ فُلانٍ" (so-and-so's soul departed) and "في نَفْسِ فُلانٍ أنْ يَفْعَلَ كَذا وكَذا" (it is in so-and-so's mind to do such-and-such). The other way: the meaning of "اَلنَّفْسُ" in it is the totality of the thing and the reality of the thing: "قَتَلَ فُلانٌ نَفْسَهُ" (so-and-so killed himself) and "أهْلَكَ فُلانٌ نَفْسَهُ" (so-and-so destroyed himself) — its meaning is not that the destruction fell upon part of him; the destruction fell only upon his entire self, and upon his reality. The meaning of "تَعْلَمُ ما في نَفْسِي" is: "You know what I conceal", "وَلا أعْلَمُ ما في نَفْسِكَ": "I do not know what is in Your reality, and that of which I have no knowledge". So the interpretation is: You know what I know, and I do not know what You know; and indicating this is ﴿إنَّكَ أنْتَ عَلامُ الغُيُوبِ﴾, for it refers back to the point concerning what is known, and to the emphasis that no one knows the unseen except Allah — exalted be His praise.

zajjaj:117-117.t: His saying: ﴿أنِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ رَبِّي ورَبَّكُمْ﴾: it is possible that "أنْ" is in the sense of "أيْ" (that is), explicative; the meaning being: "I said to them only what You commanded me, that is: worship...". It is possible that "أنْ" is in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) of the hāʾ (pronoun), "أنْ" being connected (in a ṣila) with "اُعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ", its meaning being: "except what You commanded me, (namely) that they worship Allah". And it is possible that its position is accusative as a badal of "ما", the meaning being: "I said nothing to them except: worship Allah", that is: "I mentioned to them nothing but the worship of Allah".

zajjaj:118-118.t: His saying: ﴿إنْ تُعَذِّبْهم فَإنَّهم عِبادُكَ وإنْ تَغْفِرْ لَهم فَإنَّكَ أنْتَ العَزِيزُ الحَكِيمُ﴾: the meaning of the saying of ʿĪsā — upon him be peace — "وَإنْ تَغْفِرْ لَهم": the people of reasoning differed in explaining ʿĪsā's saying "وَإنْ تَغْفِرْ لَهم". Some said: its meaning is: "If You forgive them their lying against me"; and they said: it is not permissible for ʿĪsā — upon him be peace — to say: "Allah may forgive disbelief"; so on this view it is as though (he said): "If You forgive them the report (they made) only". This is the view of Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [Translator's note: al-Mubarrad], and I do not know: is it something he heard, or did he deduce it? What I hold — and Allah knows best — is that ʿĪsā knew that among them were some who believed and some who persisted in disbelief, so ʿĪsā said about them collectively: "If You punish them", that is: "If You punish those of them who disbelieved, they are Your servants and You are just toward them, because You made the truth clear to them and they disbelieved after the argument against them had become binding; and if You forgive those of them who desisted and believed, that is a bounty from You, because it was within Your right not to accept them and not to forgive them after their enormous fabrication; and You, in Your forgiving them, are Mighty — nothing You will is beyond You — and Wise in that". Some people said: it is possible that Allah had not informed ʿĪsā that He does not forgive shirk (associating partners with Him). This is a view not worth attending to, because His saying — Exalted is He —: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَغْفِرُ أنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 48] does not single out anyone of the community of Muḥammad ﷺ to the exclusion of others, because this is a statement of fact (khabar), and a statement of fact is not abrogated. This view came up in debate, and it is not something that anyone whose knowledge is trusted believes.
